--- Page 9 ---
<meta>This page provides the Preface to the 1920 edition of the Syriac New Testament, following the printer's colophon. It details the scholarly labor and historical circumstances behind the publication, bridging the gap between G.H. Gwilliam's 1901 work and the completed volume.</meta>

## PREFACE

IN 1905 the <term>British and Foreign Bible Society</term> <note>A non-denominational charity founded in 1804 dedicated to making the Bible available throughout the world.</note> published an edition of the Gospels in Syriac, reprinted by permission from a revised text of the <term>Peshitta</term> <note>The 'Peshitta' is the standard version of the Bible for churches in the Syriac tradition; the name literally means 'simple' or 'common' version.</note> Version which had been prepared by the late Rev. G. H. Gwilliam, B.D., with a <term>Latin translation</term> <note>The original 1901 scholarly edition included Latin so that European academics who did not know Syriac could still study the text's variations.</note> and critical apparatus, and issued by the <term>Clarendon Press</term> <note>The prestigious academic imprint of Oxford University Press.</note> in 1901. To these have now been added the books from Acts to Revelation, thus completing the New Testament.

By special arrangement with the Delegates of the Clarendon Press, the text of the Acts of the Apostles, the General Epistle of James, the First Epistle General of Peter, the First Epistle General of John, and the <term>Pauline Epistles</term> <note>The letters attributed to the Apostle Paul, such as Romans and Corinthians.</note> (including Hebrews), follows a critical revision of the Peshitta originally undertaken by Mr. Gwilliam for the Clarendon Press as a completion of his edition of the Gospels (1901), and prepared on similar lines. In the collation of manuscripts at the British Museum Library, and in the correction of the proofs, the editor received assistance from the Rev. J. Pinkerton, B.D., who carried on and completed this work after Mr. Gwilliam’s death in 1913.¹ The eighteen books mentioned above are arranged in the order which is found in many of the oldest Syriac manuscripts; and the text is divided into the larger sections of the ancient Syriac system, numbering thirty-two in the Acts and the three Major <term>Catholic Epistles</term> <note>Also known as 'General Epistles,' these are New Testament letters intended for the universal church rather than a specific congregation.</note>, which are reckoned as forming one series, and fifty-five in the fourteen Pauline Epistles.

In an appendix, in order to complete the New Testament, are added the four Minor Catholic Epistles—2 Peter, 2 and 3 John, and Jude—and Revelation, which were not included in the <term>Canon of the Peshitta</term> <note>The 'Canon' refers to the official list of books accepted as Holy Scripture. The ancient Syriac church originally did not include these five books in their standard Bible.</note>.

---

¹ Mr. Pinkerton was killed in action in the Balkans, on Oct. 1, 1916. <note>John Pinkerton was a promising scholar whose life was cut short during World War I; his death delayed the completion of this project.</note> The proofs of the remaining sheets were read by the Rev. A. S. Tritton, M.A., D.Litt.

<summary>This preface outlines the editorial history of the Syriac New Testament, noting how it combined G.H. Gwilliam's earlier work with new revisions to create a complete edition. It highlights the scholarly collaboration and the tragic loss of editor John Pinkerton during World War I.</summary>

<keywords>Peshitta, G.H. Gwilliam, John Pinkerton, British and Foreign Bible Society, New Testament canon, Syriac manuscripts, World War I, Biblical scholarship</keywords>

## PREFACE

The text of **Revelation** <note>The final book of the New Testament. It is worth noting that Revelation was not included in the standard Syriac Peshitta used by early eastern churches.</note> is taken by permission from an edition issued in 1897, which was prepared by the late Rev. **John Gwynn**, D.D., <term>Regius Professor of Divinity</term> <note>A prestigious senior academic post at the University of Dublin, often appointed by the Crown.</note> at the **University of Dublin**, from a manuscript formerly in the possession of the **Earl of Crawford and Balcarres**, <note>A Scottish noble family famous for their massive private collection of rare books and manuscripts, known as the Bibliotheca Lindesiana.</note> but now preserved in the **John Rylands Library**, Manchester. The text of the **four Epistles** <note>These are 2 Peter, 2 and 3 John, and Jude. Like Revelation, these were not part of the original Syriac Peshitta canon.</note> follows the <term>Philoxenian Version</term>, <note>A very literal Syriac translation of the Bible commissioned by Philoxenus of Mabbug in 508 AD to provide a more exact rendering of the Greek original.</note> as given in **Dr. Gwynn’s** edition of *Remnants of the later Syriac Versions of the Bible*, published in 1909. For the use of these two texts the **Bible Society** is indebted to the kindness of **Dr. Gwynn**, and of the owners of the copyrights, the **Board of Trinity College, Dublin**, and the **Council of the Text and Translation Society**.

->**R. KILGOUR**,<-
->Editorial Superintendent.<-

**THE BIBLE HOUSE, LONDON,**
*December*, 1919.

<keywords>John Gwynn, Revelation, Philoxenian Version, John Rylands Library, Trinity College Dublin, Bible Society, R. Kilgour, Syriac manuscript sources</keywords>

# ܆ THE COMPLETE HISTORY ܆

## ܆ PROTONIKE THE QUEEN, DAUGHTER OF CLAUDIUS ܆
<note>Protonike is a legendary figure in Syriac tradition, often identified as the wife of the Roman Emperor Claudius. She is famously credited in these traditions with discovering the True Cross in Jerusalem prior to the more famous discovery by Empress Helena.</note>

### AND ADDAI THE APOSTLE
<note>Addai, also known as Thaddeus of Edessa, is one of the seventy disciples of Jesus. According to the "Doctrine of Addai," he was sent by the Apostle Thomas to heal King Abgar V of Edessa and evangelize the city.</note>

-> WHO IS THE BISHOP OF <term>EDESSA</term> BY THE HANDS OF <-
<note>original: "ܐܘܪܗܝ" (Urhay). This is the ancient Syriac name for Edessa, a city in modern-day Turkey that was a premier center of early Christian learning.</note>

-> NARSAI THE MONK AND TEACHER OF EDESSA ܆ <-
<note>Narsai (c. 399–502 AD) was one of the greatest poets and theologians of the Syriac tradition. Often called the "Harp of the Spirit," he led the famous School of Edessa before founding the School of Nisibis.</note>

<summary>This title page introduces the hagiographical narrative of Queen Protonike, daughter of Claudius, and her association with Addai the Apostle and the city of Edessa, as recorded or transmitted by the scholar Narsai.</summary>

# ܀ THE HOLY GOSPEL: THE PROCLAMATION OF JOHN ܀

---

<margin>Chapter 1</margin>
^1^ In the beginning <note>original: "Breshith." This is the same word used in the first verse of Genesis, intentionally linking the creation of the world to the arrival of the Word.</note> was the Word. And that Word was with God.
<margin>Of Life 1</margin>
^2^ And God was that Word. <note>original: "Miltha." While often translated as "Word" (Logos), in Syriac *Miltha* can also imply a manifestation or a concrete reality.</note> He was in the beginning with God. ^3^ Everything came to be through his hand. And without him, not even one thing came to be from that which has become. ^4^ In him was life. And the life was the light of humanity. ^5^ And that light shines in the darkness. And the darkness did not overcome it. ^6^ There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. ^7^ He came for a testimony, to testify about the light, so that everyone might believe through him. ^8^ He was not himself the light, but came to testify about the light. ^9^ For he was the light of truth, the one who enlightens every person coming into the world. ^10^ He was in the world. And the world came to be through his hand. And the world did not know him. ^11^ He came to his own, and his own did not receive him. ^12^ But those who did receive him, he gave them authority to become children of God—to those who believe in his name. ^13^ Those who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. ^14^ And the Word became flesh and dwelt <note>The Syriac term implies "pitched his tent" or "tabernacled" among us.</note> among us. And we saw his glory, glory as of the Only-Begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. ^15^ John testified about him, and cried out and said: “This is the one of whom I said: He who comes after me has become before me, because he was earlier than me.” ^16^ And from his fullness we all have received, and grace for grace. ^17^ Because the Law was given through the hand of Moses; but grace and truth came through the hand of Jesus Christ.

^18^ No one has ever seen God. The Only-Begotten God <note>The Syriac Peshitta reads "Only-Begotten God" here, whereas many English translations based on different Greek manuscripts read "Only-Begotten Son."</note> who is in the bosom of his Father, he has declared him. ^19^ And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him: “Who are you?” ^20^ And he confessed and did not deny; and he confessed: “I am not the Christ.” ^21^ And they asked him again: “What then? Are you Elijah?” And he said: “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” And he said: “No.” ^22^ And they said to him: “Then who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?” ^23^ He said: “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Straighten the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”

</note>

<margin>Chapter 2</margin>
^1^ Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the king, Magi <note>original: "Mgušē." These were scholarly priests from the East, likely Persia, skilled in astronomy and dream interpretation.</note> came from the East to Jerusalem, ^2^ saying: "Where is the King of the Jews who has been born? For we have seen his star in the East, and we have come to worship <note>The Syriac "Segda" implies physical prostration, bowing low to the ground in reverence.</note> him." ^3^ When Herod the king heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. ^4^ And he gathered all the chief priests and the scribes of the people, and he was asking them: "Where is the Messiah <note>original: "Mshikha," meaning the Anointed One.</note> to be born?" ^5^ And they said: "In Bethlehem of Judea, for so it is written in the prophet: ^6^ 'And you, Bethlehem of Judea, you were not small among the kings of Judea; for from you shall come forth a King who shall shepherd my people Israel.'" ^7^ Then Herod secretly called the Magi and learned from them at what time the star had appeared to them. ^8^ And he sent them to Bethlehem and said to them: "Go, search diligently for the child, and when you have found him, come and show me, so that I also may go and worship him." ^9^ And they, when they heard from the king, went their way. And behold, the star which they had seen in the East was going before them, until it came and stood over where the child was. ^10^ And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with very great joy. ^11^ And they entered the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and worshipped him. And they opened their treasures and offered him offerings: gold, and myrrh, and frankincense. ^12^ And it was shown to them in a dream that they should not return to Herod, and by another way they departed to their own country.܀ ܀

^13^ And when they had gone, the angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph and said to him: "Arise, take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you; for Herod is going to seek the child so as to destroy him." ^14^ Then Joseph rose, took the child and his mother by night, and departed to Egypt. ^15^ And he was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken from the Lord by the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: "Out of Egypt I have called my son."܀ ܀

^16^ Then Herod, when he saw that he had been mocked by the Magi, was very angry. And he sent and killed all the children of Bethlehem and all its borders, from two years old and under, according to the time that he had searched out from the Magi. ^17^ Then was fulfilled what was spoken by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet, who said: ^18^ "A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great lamentation; Rachel weeping for her children, and she was not willing to be comforted, because they are no more."܀ ܀ ܀

<meta>This page continues the transition from the previous "Teaching" into a specialized or commentary-heavy version of Matthew Chapter 12. While the latter half of the page aligns closely with the standard Syriac Peshitta text regarding the healing of the demoniac and the Beelzebub controversy, the first half contains unique variations—such as replacing the "sheep in a pit" with a "daughter in a snare"—suggesting this manuscript serves as a homiletic interpretation or a distinct regional recension.</meta>

-># ܀ Matthew 12 ܀<-

^9^ And he heard from the heights of darkness. And he went in his bodily form. ^10^ And there was a certain man who was saying: "I know where she is." And they were ruling over him. And they said, "They rule over me with powers over all of them," just as those who were before them said. ^11^ But he said to them: "Who is the man who loves [one] who has one **daughter** <note>original: "brata" — In the standard Gospel of Matthew 12:11, the example used is a "sheep" (erba) falling into a pit. They were paying those who rule in the path for their own renewal. ^13^ And then the man said to them: "Stretch them out." And he stretched them out. And they were [restored] according to their joy. ܀ ^14^ And the **Pharisees** <note>A Jewish sect known for strict adherence to traditional and written law; here portrayed as the primary antagonists of Jesus’s ministry.</note> went out. And he went into the midst of the empty soul, and also into his works. ^16^ And is it not written: that they should not revile him. ^17^ That they should eat his body where the Lord of breaths shall live, and he said: ^18^ And is it not written that I have delighted in him? My beloved, in whom the witnesses shall go out. ^22^ And then they brought to him a certain **demoniac** <note>original: "dywana" — one possessed by a demon.</note> who was mute and blind. And he healed him, so that the mute and blind man might speak and see. ^23^ And all the crowds were amazed. And they were saying: "Could this be the Son of David?" ^24^ But when the Pharisees heard it, they said: "This man does not cast out demons except by **Beelzebub** <term>Beelzebub: literally 'Lord of the Flies,' a name used in the New Testament for the prince of demons or Satan.</term>, the head of the demons." ^25^ But he knew their thoughts and said to them: "Every kingdom that is divided against itself shall be destroyed. And every city and house that is divided against itself shall not stand. ^26^ And if **Satan** casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. As it happened, in the fasting of pure virginity <note>The translator here seems to be providing a heading or a liturgical framing for the reading, connecting the biblical text to themes of spiritual "purity" or "fasting."</note>, let them not be empty: ^17^ Do you not know that everything which enters the mouth goes into the stomach and from there is cast out into the sewers <note>original: "ba-urokhta," literally meaning "the way" or "the passage," here referring to the natural digestive process.</note> through the natural course? ^18^ But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these are what defile a person. ^19^ For from the heart come evil thoughts: murder, adultery, fornication, theft, false witness, and blasphemy. ^20^ These are the things that defile a person; but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a person. ܀ ^21^ And Jesus went out from there and came to the region <term>region: literally "tkhuma," meaning borders or territory</term> of Tyre and Sidon. ^22^ And behold, a Canaanite woman from those regions came out and cried out, saying: "Have mercy on me, my Lord, Son of David! And his disciples approached and begged him, saying: "Send her away, for she is crying out after us." ^24^ But he answered and said: "I was not sent except to the sheep that have wandered from the house of Israel." ^25^ But she came and worshiped him, and said: "My Lord, help me." ^26^ He said to her: "It is not beautiful <note>original: "shaphir," meaning good, fair, or appropriate.</note> to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs." ^27^ But she said: "Yes, my Lord, yet even the dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters' tables." Then Jesus answered and said to her: "O woman, great is your faith! Let it be for you as you desire." And her daughter was healed from that very hour. ܀ . ܁ . ܀

^29^ And Jesus departed from there and came to the side of the Sea of Galilee, and he went up a mountain and sat there. ^30^ and many crowds approached him, and they had with them those who were lame, blind, mute, crippled <note>original: "pshikhe," which can refer to those with withered limbs or paralysis.</note>, and many others; and they laid them at the feet of Jesus, and he healed them. ^31^ So that those crowds were amazed as they saw: the mute speaking, the crippled being healed, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel. ܀ ^32^ Then Jesus called his disciples and said to them: "I have compassion for this crowd, for behold, they have remained with me for three days and they have nothing to eat. And I do not want to send them away while they are fasting <note>original: "tsaymin," used here to mean "hungry" or "without food."</note>, lest they faint on the road." ^33^ His disciples said to him: "Where can we find bread in the wilderness to satisfy such a great crowd?" ^34^ Jesus said to them: "How many loaves do you have?" They said to him: "Seven, and a few small fish." ^35^ And he commanded the crowd to sit upon the ground. ^36^ And he took those seven loaves and the fish, and he gave thanks <note>original: "shabbakh," meaning he praised or blessed.</note> and broke them, and gave them to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds. ^37^ And they all ate and were satisfied. And they took up the leftovers of the fragments, filling seven large baskets <term>large baskets: "spidin," a specific type of large wicker basket, distinct from the smaller baskets used in the feeding of the five thousand.</term>. ^38^ And those who ate were four thousand men, besides the women and children. ^39^ And when he had dismissed the crowds, he went up into a boat and came to the region of Magdala <note>original: "Magdu," identifying the town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.</note>. ܀

# ܀ Fullness ܀

<margin>Chapter 16.</margin>

1 And then sensations <term>sensations: literally "creeping things" or "feelings," referring to the basic data of the five senses</term> and agitations are dissolved for it; and they testify for it as to where there is a stable position. There is fear. 2 But that Watcher <note>original: "Ira," a term for an angel or an awakened spiritual being</note> hastens its course. When there is a constant agitation for the woman, there is fear; for it considers a stable position. 3 For its persona <term>persona: "parsopa," meaning the outward manifestation or character of a thing</term> was many-fold today. For it considers a stable position. In a fragmented way, it took stones. The persona of the stable position is an altar that is constant. And the face of the one who eats this—it is not a constant altar. 4 For its discourse is of joy, and more so like a conversation. This does not cause it to wander; rather, there is a death of the soul, and it is a grave for it. 5 And everything that belongs to Epicurus <note>original: "Abqiron," the Syriac transcription of the Greek philosopher Epicurus, known for his focus on pleasure and the avoidance of pain</note> it performs, for those who take delights for the wine. 6 And he said to them: "See, these regions are from the fields of the birds and the beehives." 7 But these stood firm in their souls; and constantly, they did not take wine. 8 But more so, he is able to hasten them: "What is our thought within your souls? Buying and considering is what exists, so that for wine there is no stable position." 9 It is not troubled by the labors of the many, nor is it in the sales of hot things for the heat of the wine of the roots; and simply, they provide a stable position. 10 And not in hard sales for the hot ones, nor the rejection of the roots; and simply, they provide a stable position. 11 So that they do not wander; and it is not concerning the wine of discernment in everything, but rather concerning the regions from the fields of the birds and the beehives. 12 And just as they wandered, he said that they should fly from the fields of wine, so as not to be from the debts of the birds and the beehives.

->܀ ܀ ܀<-

13 In it, there is a soul for the father of the birds and her holiness. It has authority over Epicurus as he hastens, because he distinguished among labors how, and in what way, and where. 14 Then you said, just as I said, the mixer is the worker. For of life, indeed, we have an Armenian movement <note>original: "Armanaya Zaw'a." This may refer to a specific school of thought or a transcription of a Greek technical term for a particular type of motion</note>. 15 See then who knows, who said in that: "For it is," because it is faithful that it is like... 16 In every work, the persona hastens, which is flying in the one who gives life to the fathers. 17 In every soul, he hastens it, for the growth of the worker as if in life; and of the witness, and the whole is not dew for us, but rather that which is cut off. 18 For we have its persona, which is a persona; and in everything, there is a distinction of life in the world and four souls. Let them not lack it. 19 For us, God is the life-giver of the worker of the cut-off; and everything that is in the four souls is also empty. And whatever is in the four souls is from delight.

->܀ ܀ ܀<-

20 And as he distinguished in Epicurus, that they should not increase without it, as it flies. 21 And from then on, the soul stood for delight in Epicurus, because in all of it, it is he who breathes into the distances. And it suffers much from the stable position and every agitation of sensations, and the descents and the fallings; and we shall kiss the wine of the fathers. 22 And this one distinguished and sanctified all of them in it. He hastens. See for us something, as to how it becomes for us. 23 But you were saved, the persona hastens; but for us, in the stealth of the garment... and how it is in him, for there is no worker for the fathers, except us, how? 24 And how does the soul speak in Epicurus? Who is great?

### ܀ Discourse 8 ܀

That I have chosen the prophets in their moments <term>moments: literally "blinkings" or "flashes," referring to the brief instances of divine inspiration</term>. And let hearing be granted. And that I have chosen from the inquiries of the judge, let the prophecy be understood. And he who sought the prophecy will find it revealed. ^26 For the Lord, for the sake of hearing—if he calls him to the work—will show the prophecy to him. ^27 O Lord, guard the prophecy that is held, and the prophecy <margin>27</margin> in that building. For the Son, who is truly of God, is in a single revelation: God, whose messenger-ship <note>original: "mal’akūtēh," referring to his mission or divine agency</note> is our Savior. And let there be prophecy for those who are silent in revelation. <margin>28</margin> ^28 They say: "I am in the midst of the prophecy of those who are holy." So that they might not be delivered to death by descending into Gehenna <note>Gehenna: the place of judgment or punishment in the afterlife</note> for those who are in her kingdom.

<margin>Chapter 17.</margin> ^1 And a true refuge they shall establish, for the Only-begotten <term>Only-begotten: "Yīḥīdāyā," a title for Christ emphasizing his unique relationship with the Father</term> Son is sheltered in his kingdom forever and ever. And he healed. (If) Gehenna is a righteous garden <note>This may be a rhetorical paradox or a scribal error comparing the punishment of the wicked to a garden for the righteous</note> for them. ^2 And how shall we hear of the living nature <note>original: "ḥayūtā," can mean vitality or animal nature</note> for its sake? He brought the discerners like a mark. But the joyful shall seize it like the light. ^3 And there is in him a strange joy, where everyone is gathered in his mouth. ^4 But the fruit enters constantly into life. The Lord went out with that people, that they might exist. We, who have received mercy, will be built up by them. God is one with them because of them, and he rejoices in the gift of God. ^5 And that which is completed—and thus let it be with God’s messenger-ship—a voice came from the creation that said: "If everything is produced that was with God, it is broken in him."

^6 And this is from what was in him of sin, which broke out in this way; and it is good gold. ^7 And let us hear the ship from the flow of sin, and it broke in it. And he said: "A standing that we did not know." ^8 And even from the joy in sin—that which he does not see—but rather in the life is the joy of that place. ^9 And they shall descend from the mountain. He cuts them off, let us hear. And he said in it: "Indeed, search, and he will show us no standing." In which he might keep silent, that he is the Son of God from the Holy One. ^10 And the fulfillment that is in life, let them understand in him. The Lord who turned back—how did they understand? Those for whom it is not right to judge in life. ^11 My sons, let us hear and say: "As he is with me, now God sanctifies us." ^12 They say: "Now, within that which belongs to God." And they shall not hear. And within him are the word and the earth. And he calls him the "Son of God" by means of life. ^13 And Adam was made equal to sin, so that they might not remain standing in the kingdom of the Lord in him.

^14 And that which he said regarding Noah: the Lord in him performs everything again in sinfulness <note>referring to the state of the world during the generation of the Flood</note>. ^15 And he said in it: "Lord, if you go out from it, by which the Son of the soul is in his sin." For the Lord Abraham was broken and went out <note>referring to Abraham leaving his homeland</note>. And God called to the sons of men. ^16 And he turned to him for his messenger-ship. And he was not found in his messenger-ship. ^17 My sons, let us hear. And he said: "If a man (if) does not know the Lord and his messenger-ship, then God is by means of sin to God." That they might be silent; for the sin of both of them is in the hand of the Son. ^18 And he calls him "Let us hear." And the holy ones shall go out from it. And he said to the sons of Noah concerning that flood. ^19 And Adam sinned in sin; the Son, let us hear in life. And he said to him: "One external life was not found in his sin." ^20 They say: "Let us hear." Because they did not participate, now in him.

¹⁴ Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you shut the **Kingdom of Heaven** before men. For you do not enter yourselves, and those who are entering, you do not allow to enter.

### -> The Revelation of John <-

That I number among all. And in this manner the numbering of the firstborn. The offspring is in him. and in the holy one who is all from him. ²¹ And thus it is delivered: the offspring among the **Cherubim** <note>Celestial beings often depicted as guardians or throne-bearers of God.</note> and the likenesses, and they number in all that is of the high creation.

²³ This is the **hanging testimony** <note>original: "Tulyaya Sahdutha" — likely a specific liturgical or poetic form where verses are "hung" or suspended in a rhythmic structure.</note> of the Saviors. The followers of Jesus <term>Yeshu'aye</term> <note>A specific term for Christians or those following the way of Jesus.</note> in the crucified one. And they are the blessed ones: the offspring, the accepted, and the acceptance. And their commandments are the honors of prayer, of knowledge, of nature, and of faith. And as if they would not be comforted; and thus they were not found; ²⁴ opposing stripes, which prosper the stroke, and fair enemies.

²⁵ This is the hanging testimony of the Saviors. The followers of Jesus in the crucified one, whom the Son and his Father prosper. But why does the beast and the written one believe? ²⁶ Outer distinctions. The generation of the firstborn, the Son of the Creator and his Father, who became also the Son of the Creator.

²⁷ This is the hanging testimony of the Saviors. The followers of Jesus in the crucified one. For they subdue them in the holy mind. And from the house of beautiful **brotherly-love** <note>original: "mayahuta" — a term emphasizing fraternal affection or the community of believers.</note>. But from his Son they believe in the fear of the person <term>qnoma</term> <note>The underlying substance or specific personhood of the Divine.</note>, and the Creator of the resurrection. ²⁸ And they are the faith from the house of brotherly-love; they were comforted in the crucified one. And from his Son they believe in the cross of the crucified.

²⁹ This is the hanging testimony of the Saviors. The followers of Jesus in the crucified one. For they are the building of the holy and righteous ones. And they prosper by the knowledge of the confessors of the crucified. ³⁰ And they were comforted, those who conquered the lower gardens through them. But holiness is not in them among the crucified righteous ones. ³¹ Therefore he confesses them in the absence of self. For they are the sons who were made to rejoice in the crucified. ³² And even they, the perfect king of the fathers. ³³ The beasts, the Lord of the crucified. Just as they are from the person <note>original: "qnoma"</note> itself.

³⁴ Because of this, I do not perish in prayer. Stripes and beasts. Testimonies. # Doctrine #

In it, <term>my Lord</term> <note>Syriac: "Mari" — a title of respect for a teacher or a divine address</note> says that in that state they were not created. And regarding the Creator: if these evils which were crucified against Him were purifiers for Him, then before the peace of the <term>angels</term> <note>Syriac: "malake" — messengers or celestial beings</note>, let all life be discerning. For He spoke to these with the voice of the three. ⁴⁶ And to the three thousand angels, He lifted their hands in the righteous division. All these are ministering spirits. ⁴⁷ Moreover, they were gathered again from those who had fallen from the three; when the angel came from them in silence, the three were fulfilled. ⁴⁸ And in this fulfillment, one <term>Sun</term> <note>Syriac: "Shemsha" — likely a metaphor for Christ as the spiritual light-source</note> came to be, and it took again one Sun. And He brought forth one <term>side</term> <note>Syriac: "geba" — can mean a side, a party, or a wing of an army/angelic host</note>, and divided one side, and brought down one side; and the temple was like an angel from them. ⁴⁹ The root, then, was repeated, along with the truth. Let us see if the side was in the midst of creation; ⁵⁰ however, let him be silent like a completely righteous angel, even as you are. ⁵¹ And in the righteous support of the three—for you are in the three—from the world. Therefore, creation shall be renewed. And He brought out the three thousand. ⁵² And in that portion of the place of <term>Zion</term> <note>Zion is used here as a mystical location of divine presence</note>, He divided the portion of the place of heaven, and brought down the portion of the place of earth. ⁵³ And He brought out the three thousand among angelic humans; and the number of the place that ascended was fulfilled in humanity. ⁵⁴ All those who had fallen were of the side. And there was peace among them. Who is the living one from the living ones who are in heaven and on earth? For there is peace, and God, and the showing of the three, if it was fulfilled in the three. ⁵⁵ If from the living ones of the earth, He shall bring out the three thousand, that they might be in humanity, in the matter, so that God might be silent from within humanity. And He shall fulfill in humanity the side that had fallen, ⁵⁶ which he saw in the three: the angel, the human, and the showing. And they shall be silent unto the five because of His word, when I have fulfilled it.

⁵⁷ From within humanity, however, you said: "How shall it be known, and from what?" He who fulfills the completion—since I also was known— ⁵⁸ that the three of us are fulfilled in this way. And He shall show us that God was in us, ⁵⁹ fulfilling the completion and the showing of the three which took place on earth. And He took from us in humanity and brought forth the <term>body</term> <note>Syriac: "paghra" — the physical or incarnate body</note>, ⁶⁰ and they ascended to heaven. ⁶¹ And in this side they were known: that he brought to the earth of heaven, and took from us five, and fulfilled them in the three.

⁶² Regarding those of heaven: how shall we know that He fulfills these words? Was it not God ⁶³ who in the five became an angel? And those of the Creator, just as he became: "I am the <term>Son of Man</term>." And He brought out the side, ⁶⁴ and ascended from us in humanity. Earth and heaven—just as God was repeated—were fulfilled. And the showing of the three, as you said: He took the side and brought out the side. ⁶⁵ This happened for us, just as I am five from five. ⁶⁶ And He took them as a side, and brought them out as a side, just as God fulfilled.

### ܀ The Holy Gospel, the Proclamation of Matthew ܀ ###

<margin>Chapter 1</margin>
¹ The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
² Abraham fathered Isaac; Isaac fathered Jacob; Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers. ³ Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez fathered Hezron; Hezron fathered Aram. ⁴ Aram fathered Amminadab; Amminadab fathered Nahshon; Nahshon fathered Salmon. ⁵ Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab; Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth; Obed fathered Jesse. ⁶ Jesse fathered David the king; David fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah. ⁷ Solomon fathered Rehoboam; Rehoboam fathered Abijah; Abijah fathered Asa. ⁸ Asa fathered Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat fathered Joram; Joram fathered Uzziah. ⁹ Uzziah fathered Jotham; Jotham fathered Ahaz; Ahaz fathered Hezekiah. ¹⁰ Hezekiah fathered Manasseh; Manasseh fathered Amon; Amon fathered Josiah. ¹¹ Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the <term>exile</term> <note>Syriac: "galuta" — referring to the forced deportation of the Jews to Babylon.</note> to Babylon.

¹² And after the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel; Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel. ¹³ Zerubbabel fathered Abiud; Abiud fathered Eliakim; Eliakim fathered Azor. ¹⁴ Azor fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Achim; Achim fathered Eliud. ¹⁵ Eliud fathered Eleazar; Eleazar fathered Matthan; Matthan fathered Jacob. ¹⁶ Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called the <term>Messiah</term> <note>Syriac: "Mshikha" — the Anointed One.</note>.

¹⁷ Thus, all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the exile to Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the exile to Babylon until the Messiah are fourteen generations.

¹⁸ Now the birth of Jesus Christ was in this way: While Mary his mother was betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be pregnant from the <term>Holy Spirit</term> <note>Syriac: "Rukha d-Qudsha." In Syriac, "Spirit" is often treated as a feminine noun, reflecting early Eastern Christian traditions.</note>. ¹⁹ But Joseph her husband was a righteous man, and he did not wish to expose her, so he intended to release her secretly. ²⁰ But while he was considering these things, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said to him, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your wife, for that which is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. ²¹ She will bear a son, and you shall call his name <term>Jesus</term> <note>Syriac: "Yeshu" — a name related to the root meaning "to save" or "deliverer."</note>, for he will save his people from their sins."

²² Now all this happened so that what was spoken from the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled: ²³ "Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Immanuel," which is translated as, "Our God is with us." ²⁴ When Joseph rose from his sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and he took his wife.

### ܀ Mark 2 ܀ ###

Jesus said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him? <sup>25</sup> <note>Original: "ܩܪܰܝܬ݁ܽܘܢ" (qrayton) - 'Have you read'. <sup>29</sup> And he entered the synagogue again, and a certain man was there whose hand was withered. <sup>30</sup> And they were watching him to see if he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him. <sup>31</sup> And he said to the man whose hand was withered, "Stand in the middle." <sup>32</sup> And he said to them as well, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil? <sup>35</sup> <note>The verse numbering resets/overlaps here as the text transitions to Mark 1:35.</note> And in the morning, long before it was light, he rose and went to a deserted place, and there he was praying. <sup>36</sup> And Simon and those with him searched for him. <sup>37</sup> And when they found him, they said to him, "Everyone is looking for you." <sup>38</sup> He said to them, "Come, let us go to the nearby villages and towns, so that I may preach there also; for this is why I have come." <sup>39</sup> And he was preaching in all their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and casting out demons. <sup>40</sup> And a <term>leper</term> <note>Syriac: "ܓ݁ܰܪܒ݂ܳܐ" (garba). You cannot serve God and <term>Mammon</term><note>A Semitic term for money or material wealth, often personified as a false god.</note>. 25 Because of this, I say to you: do not be anxious for your life, what you will eat and what you will drink: nor for your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food: and the body more than clothing? 26 Look at the birds of the sky: for they do not sow, nor do they reap, nor do they gather into storehouses: and your Father who is in heaven feeds them. Are you not more important than they? 27 And who among you by being anxious: is able to add one cubit to his stature? 28 And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field: how they grow: they do not toil and they do not spin. 29 But I say to you: that even Solomon in all his glory: was not clothed like one of these. 30 Now if God so clothes the grass of the field: which today is, and tomorrow falls into the oven: how much more you, O you of little faith. 31 Therefore, do not be anxious or say: what will we eat or what will we drink or what will we wear. 32 For the Gentiles seek all these things. But your Father who is in heaven knows: that you also need all these things. 33 But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness: and all these things will be added to you. 34 Therefore, do not be anxious about tomorrow: for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

# ⁜ The First Account: The Creation of the World ⁜

<margin>Chapter 1</margin>
^1^ In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. ^2^ And the earth was formless and void <note>original: *tuh w-buh*, a Syriac rendering of the Hebrew *tohu wa-bohu*, describing primeval chaos</note>. And darkness was over the face of the abyss, and the Spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters. ^3^ And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light. ^4^ And God saw the light, that it was good; and God divided the light from the darkness. ^5^ And God called the light "Day" and the darkness He called "Night." And there was evening and there was morning, day one.

->⁜<-

^6^ And God said, "Let there be an expanse <term>expanse: *raqio*, the dome or "firmament" of the sky that ancient people believed held back the upper waters</term> in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters." ^7^ And God made the expanse, and divided the waters which were under the expanse from the waters which were above the expanse; and it was so. ^8^ And God called the expanse "Heaven." And there was evening and there was morning, the second day.

->⁜<-

^9^ And God said, "Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together into one place, and let the dry land appear"; and it was so. ^10^ And God called the dry land "Earth," and the gathering together of the waters He called "Seas"; and God saw that it was good.

->⁜<-

^11^ And God said, "Let the earth sprout sprouts of grass that produces seed, and fruit trees that yield fruit according to their kind, whose seed is in them, upon the earth"; and it was so. ^12^ And the earth brought forth sprouts of grass that produces seed according to its kind, and trees that yield fruit whose seed is in them, according to their kind; and God saw that it was good. ^13^ And there was evening and there was morning, the third day.

->⁜<-

^14^ And God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs and for seasons and for days and for years. ^15^ And let them be for lights in the expanse of heaven to give light upon the earth"; and it was so. ^16^ And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; and also the stars. ^17^ And God set them in the expanse of heaven to give light upon the earth, ^18^ and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness; and God saw that it was good. ^19^ And there was evening and there was morning, the fourth day.

->⁜<-

^20^ And God said, "Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures <term>living creatures: *napsha hayta*, literally "living soul," used here for marine life</term>, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of heaven." ^21^ And God created the great sea monsters <note>original: *tanyane*, referring to massive sea creatures or legendary dragons</note> and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind; and God saw that it was good. ^22^ And God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth." And there was evening and there was morning, the fifth day.

<gloss>4</gloss> It is written, as it says in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah: "The voice of one calling in the wilderness: <note>original: *ḥurbā*, meaning a dry, desolate place or desert</note> Prepare the way of the Lord, and make straight his paths in the plain for our God. <gloss>5</gloss> All the valleys shall be filled, and all the mountains and hills shall be brought low. $^{21}$ ...that was in him. And she <note>Likely referring to the Virgin Mary or the Church personified as the soul.</note> stood in her initial virginity. We have spoken of how this is written in its proper place. $^{22}$ And our testimony becomes a narration for her. All of it becomes symbolic of the nature that went out from his mouth. And he was at rest <note>original: *ethniḥ*. In Syriac spirituality, "rest" refers to a state of divine peace or the indwelling of the Spirit.</note>. This was not merely a product of thought, $^{23}$ but it was her very soul, within that which was extended from her. Just as your soul became, and every form within her was in the nature of the **Trinity**; for this also exists in the state of Messiah-hood <note>original: *mshikhayutha*. This term can mean "Christianity" or the "Anointed state" of Christ.</note>. 

$^{24}$ It is like a discourse which says that he saw this within her: who is it that wanders and is killed in Messiah-hood? $^{25}$ For truly it said within her, "I have been greatly extended by their hands," in the life of those deceivers. When our soul was recounted by us as three members and three paths: where the male body was within the female body. $^{26}$ And beyond her, joy was not found for the soul, except in the righteousness of the struggle, in which she was humbled and transformed. 

$^{27}$ And these delights were revealed from her, which were in Messiah-hood. In the life of the healthy one, the soul grew; she who is faithful was not deceived, except if she finds sweetness in righteousness. $^{28}$ This glorifies our Lord, even as though toward an enemy; for he was glorified in the bodily placement. $^{29}$ And he is able to be glorified for her salvation; the enemy is somewhat inclined, and it was recounted at the time to the Galilee that is outside. For he is her height, a light <note>original: *gayra*, literally an arrow or a ray of light.</note> in the totality of the soul, so that transformations might be found from her. $^{30}$ But in all her knowledge, he was at rest. 

$^{31}$ And like a proverb, she leans toward her salvation, that of our soul. And he was at rest in two buildings <note>A metaphor likely referring to the two natures of Christ or the soul and body.</note>. $^{32}$ And she was being saved in both of them, all of her in the **Trinity** of the Messiah, becoming an angel. ♱ ♱ 

$^{33}$ And as if he became an enemy—a light <note>or "arrow"</note> that was in him. And he saw that the light had come. And he called out with a loud voice and said: something primary <note>or "ancient"</note>. "What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? ... You have come to us to destroy our souls." <note>This is a direct citation of the demon's cry in Mark 1:24 and Luke 4:34.</note> $^{34}$ See now, is this not the salvation of God? 

$^{35}$ And your soul marveled at him and said: "From here is salvation! And the salvation of all!" And the holy apostleship is in the inclination, and it went out from her. For in purity, he does not bear witness in him from her. $^{36}$ And just as it was according to her nature, it became complete. Rather, he is the life and he was at rest. Who is the angel in him that became? For he placed a mark upon them, and with power the body is in the life of the soul and its departure. 

$^{37}$ And the good enemy <note>Perhaps referring to the "adversary" who unwittingly serves God's plan.</note> departed in her body, which came by his names. ♱ $^{38}$ And he—her soul departed from the enemy. In all the nature of your soul and its perfected warmth. For where it was in the hands of the body, and in everything was its rest. And he stood as vinegar <note>or "strength"</note> from her; and he marveled at the hands of her salvation and her completion. And from his holy and perfected hand, it came to be in her. ♱ 

$^{39}$ The perfected angel that came to be: in two ways, just as he came, just as he was in that building which was before him. ♱ $^{40}$ Rest is found, however, in those things: just as he came, just as he was in that building which was before him, the perfected building before him, just as it was in his place. 

$^{41}$ But the body went out from the delights, from his life. And he was at rest. For where are the hands in him, those of God? And he marveled that he was in his place. And he does not leave what was in his place, and the rest in both of them is in him. $^{42}$ And as he was in his place, he was found in both of them, that he was in his place, in his place. $^{43}$ It is like the discourse which says that he was in him. And also in the perceptions of the soul, upon which he placed a mark. $^{44}$

¹² And it happened that while Jesus was in one of the cities, a man came who was completely full of leprosy. And they were filled with fear, and said, "We have seen wonders today."

# ### Tablet 9 ###

⁴¹ And a certain man whose name was John <note>Syriac: *Yohannan*. Given the context, this could refer to John the Apostle or John the Baptist, though the mystical setting suggests the "Beloved Disciple" tradition.</note> was fragrant with it. Something fell into the heart of Simon, and he was seeking from him that he might prepare his legion. ⁴² But the man was of noble lineage. Like a creature stretched out was the **Aranitha** <term>Aranitha: A difficult term, likely referring to a mystical vessel, an ark, or a spiritual "receptacle" used in the sanctuary</term>. And he was holy to receive it. And when John came to its place, the man rejoiced greatly in him.

⁴³ But how did he live and endure from that very **Aranitha**, when his face fell into the midst of the papal cloisters? <note>The term *qinayatha* refers to nests or small monastic cells/cloisters.</note> And he was not struck by those **Aranithas**. ⁴⁴ And he promised of his own will, and he offered the wagon and all that was in it. And his voice strikes the demons who are afraid.

⁴⁵ And John said: "What and how then?" And from the mouth of Simon, he said to him: "The fruit and the garment are in conflict. Go, the guests <note>Literally "those reclining at a banquet"</note> are waiting for you and your companions." ⁴⁶ And John said: "What and how then? These are but one thing. For I know that the knowledge of the sand <note>Or "vinegar" (*hala*), possibly a metaphor for the bitterness of worldly knowledge or the foundational nature of sand</note> has fallen from me." ⁴⁷ "Lord, how then shall we live without conflict? For there is great revelation to him. And the building gazes upon the fruit: the hand of the holy man is placed there. And how does the **Aranitha** strike?" ⁴⁸ This, then, if it is served—to whom does it belong? Nothing but the external lie... and it strikes a trembling into Satan like a flame.

⁴⁹ And in that very thing he spoke: but when he is served from the blood, John is for him. A savior to him is the heat—not man, nor divinity in the exodus <note>Syriac: *mapoqana*, which can mean a liturgical procession, the exit of the soul from the body, or the biblical Book of Exodus</note>. ⁵⁰ More than the heat is John of the garment, of the garment. Not God, but a man who was struck, and lived. ⁵¹ But the man is indeed served. And he did not know that love was his garment. But rather to serve, and to be served, and to counsel, and for the memorial of the garment. And God. ⁵² The fruit, moreover, is his man. And a man came from him. John, however, was his own; not God, not all fruit, but he who was a man. ⁵³ And a striking occurred in his heart, regarding the judgment of the **Aranitha**. ⁵⁴ These are the external garments, and the kinship is in the hand. And John called her to receive. He burned the altar, ⁵⁵ and he commanded its smoke and struck its voice. And he clapped his hands in that exodus. ⁵⁶ And his face was opened to Satan. These things are the judgment of her weariness. Not all is the knowledge of God.

<sup>42</sup> And our Lord said: "Who then is the faithful and wise steward <note>original: *rabbaitā*, a household manager or overseer</note>, whom his lord shall appoint over his servants, to give them their portion of food in its season? <sup>43</sup> Blessed is that servant whom his lord, when he comes, shall find so doing. <sup>44</sup> Truly I say to you, that he will appoint him over all his possessions. <sup>45</sup> But if that servant says in his heart, 'My lord delays his coming,' and begins to beat the male and female servants of his lord, and begins to eat and drink and become drunk, <sup>46</sup> the lord of that servant will come on a day he does not expect, and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him asunder, and appoint his portion with those who are unfaithful. <sup>47</sup> And that servant who knew his lord's will, yet did not prepare for him according to his will, shall receive many stripes <note>A reference to lashes or a beating as a form of judicial punishment</note>. <sup>48</sup> But he who did not know, yet did things worthy of stripes, shall receive few stripes. $^{11}$ "Now this is the parable: The seed is the word of God. $^{12}$ Those by the wayside are those who hear the word, but the Accuser <note>original: "Akel-qarsa" – literally "the eater of pieces," a common Syriac term for the Devil or Slanderer</note> comes and takes the word from their heart, so that they might not believe and be saved. $^{13}$ Those upon the rock are those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but they have no root, and their faith is only for a time, and in a time of trial they stumble. $^{14}$ That which fell among thorns are those who hear the word, but by the cares and wealth and desires of the world they are choked, and they yield no fruit. $^{15}$ But that in the good ground are those who, with a beautiful and good heart, hear the word and hold it fast, and yield fruit with patience.

$^{16}$ "No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel, or puts it under a bed. Instead, he puts it upon a lampstand, so that whoever enters may see its light. $^{17}$ For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything concealed that will not be known and come into the open. $^{18}$ Take heed how you hear. For to him who has, more will be given; and from him who has not, even that which he thinks he has will be taken away."

$^{19}$ Then his mother and his brothers came to him, but they were not able to speak with him because of the crowd. $^{20}$ And they said to him, "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside and wish to see you." $^{21}$ But he answered and said to them, "These are my mother and my brothers: those who hear the word of God and do it."

$^{22}$ And it happened on one of those days that Jesus went up and sat in a boat <term>boat (Syriac: saphinta): a common fishing vessel used on the Sea of Galilee</term>, he and his disciples. And a windstorm arose on the lake, and the boat was near to sinking. $^{24}$ And they approached and woke him, saying to him, "Our Master, our Master, we are perishing!" But they, being afraid, were amazed and said to one another, "Who then is this, that he commands even the winds and the waves and the water, and they obey him?"

$^{26}$ And they sailed and came to the region of the Gaderenes, which is on the side opposite Galilee. $^{27}$ And when he went out to the land, a certain man from the city met him, who had demons in him for a long time. And he wore no clothes, and did not live in a house, but in the place of the tombs. $^{28}$

<meta>This page continues the interpretive commentary following the narrative of Luke 18 and 19. While the previous page focused on the Gospel text itself, this page shifts into a dense theological reflection on the nature of Christ’s "Person" (Parsopa) and "Body" (Pagra), using analogies like the sun and its rays to explain the relationship between the Father and the Son.</meta>

### ܀ Plate 9 ܀

<gloss>14</gloss> Our God, the one who created everything from nothing, we believe that they exist. Apart from him, there is nothing. And his necessary <note>original: "eltsoya" — meaning essential or compelled by nature</note> Person <note>original: "parsopa" — a technical term in Syriac theology referring to the individual manifestation or "mask" of a person, especially used to describe the union of Christ’s natures</note> is perfect and outgoing. # ܀ The Holy Gospel, the Preaching of John ܀

<margin>Chapter 1</margin> ¹ In the beginning was the Word <note>original: "Miltha." This Syriac term is equivalent to the Greek "Logos," referring to the divine reason or person of Christ.</note>. And that Word was with God. And God was that Word. ² This one was in the beginning with God. ³ Everything came to be through his hand; and without him, not even one thing came to be that has come to be. ⁴ In him was life, and the life was the light of the sons of men. ⁵ And that light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome <note>Or "comprehend/extinguish."</note> it.

⁶ There was a man who was sent from God, his name was John. ⁷ This one came for testimony, to testify concerning the light, so that everyone might believe through his hand. ⁸ He was not the light, but [was sent] to testify concerning the light. ⁹ For he was the light of truth, which gives light to everyone who comes into the world. ¹⁰ He was in the world, and the world came to be through his hand, and the world did not know him. ¹¹ He came to his own, and his own did not receive him. ¹² But those who did receive him, he gave them authority to become the children of God—to those who believe in his name. ¹³ Those who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.

¹⁴ And the Word became flesh and dwelt <note>literally: "pitched his tent" or "tabernacled."</note> among us, and we saw his glory, glory as of the Only-begotten <note>original: "Yakhidaya," meaning unique or only-begotten.</note> from the Father, full of grace and truth. ¹⁵ John testified concerning him and cried out and said: "This is the one of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me was before me, because he was earlier than me.’" ¹⁶ And from his fullness we have all received, and grace for grace. ¹⁷ Because the Law was given through the hand of Moses, but truth and grace came through Jesus Christ <note>original: "Isho Mshikha."</note>. ¹⁸ No man has ever seen God; the Only-begotten God <note>Many Syriac manuscripts, following the Peshitta tradition, read "Only-begotten God" rather than "Only-begotten Son" here.</note>, he who is in the bosom of his Father, he has declared him.

¹⁹ And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent to him from Jerusalem priests and Levites to ask him: "Who are you?" ²⁰ And he confessed and did not deny; he confessed: "I am not the Messiah." ²¹ And they asked him again: "What then? Are you Elijah?" and he said, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet?" and he said, "No." ²² And they said to him: "Who then are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say concerning yourself?" ²³ He said: "I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said."

²⁴ Now those who were sent were from the Pharisees. ²⁵ And they asked him and said to him: "Why then do you baptize if you are not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?" ²⁶ John answered and said to them: "I baptize with water; but among you stands one whom you do not know. ²⁷ This is the one who comes after me and was before me, the one whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie."

# JOHN

<margin>Chapter 10</margin>
$^1$“Truly, truly <note>original: "Amen, amen." A solemn formula used by Jesus to emphasize the absolute truth of the following statement</note>, I say to you: he who does not enter the sheepfold through the gate, but climbs up from another place, is a thief and a bandit. $^2$But he who enters through the gate is the shepherd of the flock. $^3$To him the gatekeeper opens the door, and the flock hears his voice. He calls his own sheep by their names and leads them out. $^4$And when he has brought out his flock, he goes before it, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice. $^5$But the flock does not follow a stranger; rather, it flees from him, because it does not recognize the voice of a stranger.” $^6$Jesus spoke this parable <note>original: "palātā," which can mean a proverb, a metaphor, or a veiled illustration</note> to them, but they did not understand what he was saying to them. $^7$So Jesus said to them again: “Truly, truly, I say to you: I am the gate of the flock. $^8$All those who came before are thieves and bandits, but the flock did not listen to them. $^9$I am the gate. If anyone enters by me, he will live; he will go in and go out and find pasture. $^{10}$A thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I have come so that they might have life, and that they might have it in abundance. $^{11}$I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his flock. $^{12}$But a hireling <note>original: "agirā," a hired laborer who works for wages rather than out of ownership or love</note>, who is not the shepherd and does not own the sheep, when he sees a wolf coming, leaves the flock and flees. Then the wolf snatches and scatters the flock. $^{13}$The hireling flees because he is a hireling and does not care for the flock. $^{14}$I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I am known by my own. $^{15}$Just as my Father knows me, I also know my Father; and I lay down my life for the flock. $^{16}$And I have other sheep which are not from this fold <note>original: "ṭyrā," referring to the enclosure or pen. This is often interpreted as a reference to the Gentiles</note>. I must bring them in also, and they will hear my voice. The entire flock shall become one, and there shall be one shepherd. $^{17}$Because of this my Father loves me: because I lay down my life so that I may take it up again. $^{18}$No one takes it from me; rather, I lay it down of my own will. For I have the power to lay it down, and I have the power to take it up again. This command I received from my Father.” $^{19}$There was again a division among the Jews because of these words. $^{20}$Many of them were saying, “He has a demon and is insane! Why do you listen to him?” $^{21}$But others were saying, “These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”

->܀<-

$^{22}$Then the Feast of Dedication <note>original: "tagdidtā," referring to Hanukkah, the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem</note> took place in Jerusalem. It was winter, $^{23}$and Jesus was walking in the Temple, in the Portico of Solomon <note>original: "esṭwā d-Shlemon," a covered colonnade on the eastern side of the Temple mount</note>. $^{24}$The Jews gathered around him and said to him, “How long will you keep our souls in suspense? If you are the Christ <note>original: "Mshiḥā," the Anointed One/Messiah</note>, tell us plainly.” $^{25}$Jesus answered and said to them, “I have told you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in the name of my Father bear witness to me. $^{26}$But you do not believe because you are not of my sheep, $^{27}$just as I told you. My sheep hear my voice; I know them, and they follow me.”

This is the **Chosen Christ**. ^32^ "And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, ^[32]^ I am the Savior of the world." ^33^ And this he said, signifying by what death he would die. ^34^ The crowds answered him: "We have heard from the Law <note>The 'Law' refers to the Torah or the Hebrew Scriptures</note> that the Christ remains forever. You say that he who is from the earth must be lifted up. And like a grieving word: "And the God of gods is from them."

^37^ And that which is from our heart, the redeemer of the place, his **holy chosen ones**, let it not be poor of mouth. ^38^ For you are the **fatness of Christ** <note>original: "helbe d-mshiha," likely a metaphor for the richness of grace or the 'milk' of basic teaching</note> which you have filled in the years. The word of my fathers which says: "They shall live." ^40^ Their children bought his honor forever, so that they would not sin in their sins and be emptied in their world; and they shall be saved even they themselves. ^41^ And he said: "I have fulfilled [it]." One of his chariots, and the word of their world.

^42^ Also from the name of these treasures, he took from it. And he said: "Whoever serves me, shall not be serving in me, but in the heart of the demons." <note>This appears to be an interpretive warning against false service</note> ^45^ And whoever mocks the Lord, his joy is in the mouth of demons. ^46^ "I have come as a **light into the world**, so that whoever serves me shall not fall into darkness. ^47^ And whoever hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world. ^48^ Whoever rejects me and does not receive my words, has one who judges him. The word that I have spoken, that will judge him on the last day. ^49^ For I have not spoken from myself, but the Father who sent me gave me a commandment—what I should say and what I should speak. ^50^ And I know that his commandment is **eternal life**. Therefore, the things that I speak, just as my Father told me, so I speak."

<margin>Chapter 21</margin>
^1 After these things, Jesus showed himself again to his disciples by the Sea of Tiberias <note>Also known as the Sea of Galilee</note>. He showed himself in this way: ^2 They were all together: Simon Peter <note>original: "Shem'un Kepha"</note>, Thomas who is called the Twin <note>original: "Thama"; the Syriac word for twin</note>, Nathanael who was from Cana of Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of the disciples. ^3 Simon Peter said to them, "I am going to catch fish." They said to him, "We also are coming with you." And they went out and got into the boat, and that night they caught nothing. ^4 But when morning came, Jesus stood by the shore of the sea, and the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.

^5 Jesus said to them, "Children, do you have anything to eat?" They said to him, "No." ^6 He said to them, "Cast your net on the right side of the boat, and you will find [some]." And they cast it, and they were not able to pull the net in because of the multitude of fish they had caught. ^7 And that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "This is our Lord!" When Simon Peter heard that it was our Lord, he took his tunic and tied it around his waist—for he was naked <note>In this context, it likely means he was stripped for work, wearing only an undergarment</note>—and he threw himself into the sea to come to Jesus. ^8 But the other disciples came in the boat, for they were not far from the land, only about two hundred cubits <note>A cubit is approximately 18 inches, making this about 100 yards</note>, and they were dragging the net of fish.

^9 When they got up onto the land, they saw burning coals set out, and fish placed on them, and bread. ^10 Jesus said to them, "Bring some of those fish you have just caught now." ^11 Simon Peter went up and dragged the net to the land, full of large fish: one hundred and fifty-three. And even with such a great number, the net was not torn. ^12 Jesus said to them, "Come, have breakfast." But none of the disciples dared to ask him who he was, for they knew that it was our Lord. ^13 And Jesus approached, took the bread and the fish, and gave it to them. ^14 This was the third time Jesus appeared to his disciples after he rose from the dead.

^15 When they had finished breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon, son of Jona, do you love me more than these?" He said to him, "Yes, my Lord, you know that I love you." He said to him, "Feed my lambs." ^16 He said to him again a second time, "Simon, son of Jona, do you love me?" He said to him, "Yes, my Lord, you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Tend my sheep <note>original: "urbane"; specifically referring to young sheep or rams</note>." ^17 He said to him a third time, "Simon, son of Jona, do you love me?" And it grieved Peter that he said to him a third time, "Do you love me?" And he said to him, "My Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Feed my ewes <note>original: "neqwatan"; the Syriac Peshitta uses three different words for the flock in this dialogue</note>." ^18 "Truly, truly I say to you: when you were young, you used to gird your own waist and walk where you wished. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird your waist and take you where you do not wish." ^19 He said this to show by what kind of death he was to glorify God.

# ܀ Preface ܀
## Of the Apostolic Discourses for the Solitaries

<margin>Chapter 1</margin>
¹ The first part begins with He who is: the first King of the beautiful ones, my Lord Jesus. ² Therefore, to aid the joys of the Kingdom, He existed in the likeness of the structures <note>original: "banyatha"; in Syriac mystical literature, this refers to the "edifices" or internal spiritual constructions of the soul</note> to which He was bound, more than any single breath. ³ Let Him go forth to be like a promise; those who are of the body today and of the resurrection. And just as some among them shall go forth in prayer from every worldly governance, so in many likenesses shall many be in the unity of the Kingdom. For the Kingdom has come to be within them, just like all the governance of the earth. ⁴ Thus, let it not be for the sake of the holy one to go out as if he were in bondage, but rather that they might go out to be the possession of the Father. And there was a speaking of the word from Him. ⁵ And he changed the hospitality <note>original: "aksenya"; from the Greek "xenia," meaning the state of being a stranger or pilgrim on earth</note> of the joyful ones, and those who are in His hand, in likeness and in resurrection—not in every way, but in great abundance. ⁶ And just as it is in the likeness of His Kingdom, and as it came to be in Him, the Lord: for in this way the Kingdom exists, even as the Kingdom of the "How." ⁷ When He was within them, it was not that He became a friend who was by nature a father or a stone <note>The text here contrasts the biological or material with the spiritual relationship</note>; those of whom hope spoke from the earth in the discourse of those who went out. ⁸ But in the likeness that belongs to the resurrection, in the clothing <note>original: "labushta"; refers to the spiritual garment or "robe of glory" put on by the soul</note>; and just as some and the earth are within them in a single multitude, in the confession of the nature of the new things. And even the perfected life, and in the purity of the beauty of the earth. ⁹ Thus are those who are constant: from the life that is in the resurrection, and the firstborn children. And it is from His clothing. ¹⁰ And even the new life which was in beauty, was in Him just as He was. For the preparation of their knowledge is from them in beauty, in the new clothing. ¹¹ And just as it is within them, let it be of beauty. The first Lord, He is the new things in beauty. And like the new things of the confession of the Kingdom in beauty, and the expanse of the Father, like every new joy that came to be in beauty. ¹² and beauty came to be. And there is an opening within them for confession, from the blessedness of the resurrection of the new life. And those things which came to be in every matter of confession, and the opening from Him is like the greatness of the resurrection. ¹³ And it was in the likeness of what became the new ascended ones among them, in the structures that came to be in Him, in the clothing and in the changing, and in the perfection of what they became. And the resurrection of the likeness, and the hope in Him: that of the mind <note>original: "tar'itha"; the faculty of thought or the movement of the mind toward God</note>, and the new things are perfected in Him, and He is perfected for the second time. And just as they became perfected. ¹⁴ And as at the first: those who are new among the kindred of the Kingdom, who existed in the matter, shall go forth in unity with the life, and with the Kingdom that was changed, and with the living state. ¹⁵ And the life of the Kingdom came to be: the perfected station of the Father, the Kingdom of the end <note>original: "laphutha"; can imply the end-times or the ultimate fulfillment</note>. If it should be that they are indeed in unity, just as His entire Kingdom is. And thus: ¹⁶ those new things which... I will return so that He might nourish...

# ܀ Discourse Thirty-One ܀

Hear, O pleasant ones, of the sacrifice <note>original: "neksta" — can mean slaughter, sacrifice, or even wealth/possessions; here it refers to a spiritual offering</note> that exists in life, which is near to all existence. <sup>43</sup> It is not heard or performed with difficulty; rather, it flows in the presence of God: that which the children of the children of his fathers rely upon, which was heard by them before the time. <sup>44</sup> And oh, how pleasant is the hearing of the testimony of the fathers! This too is just as He commanded—He who spoke through the prophecies by His word, the crown of His life. <sup>45</sup> And in this hearing, it is not only His word alone that is upon the fathers through His breath; rather, there God gave them an inheritance from their children, who are the signs before Him. And it is in the likeness of the lives of the fathers: <sup>46</sup> that which resembles the service <note>original: "ḥshāḥā" — use, service, or necessity</note> of God. And all of it provides for their own fathers. <sup>47</sup> Now, as for the hearing: <sup>48</sup> it rejoices in the new thing. And this is not believed through the former work. As the prophet said: <sup>49</sup> "He who provides in my way, and eats of the sacrifice of the brothers of my body." These are in the newness of my claims <note>original: "teb‘āy" — demands, claims, or seekings</note>; for what is the Lord? Or those whom I am of life. <sup>50</sup> Not here where he lives, in the church and the dissolution of their bodies; <sup>51</sup> or the [unclear] and without their names in their hands and in their hearing... those in their body, the virginity that was, which existed from the beginning. **Key terms used:**
*   **Salvation (Purqana):** Deliverance or the act of saving.
*   **Godhead (Allāhūtā):** The essential nature of God.
*   **Testimony (Sāhdūtā):** Often implies martyrdom or a witness of faith.
*   **Fulfilling (Mšamleyn):** Completing or perfecting a task or prophecy.
*   **Wisdom (Ḥekmatā):** Divine insight.
*   **Service (Pulḥānā):** Work, labor, or liturgical worship.
*   **In time (Ba-zbanā):** At the appointed season.

### ܀ Discourse Fourteen ܀ ###

...of their robbery, how it happened. Therefore, he saw the first deed that occurred. <gloss>6</gloss> And they were hoping from the creation: that the Creator-Son established [it], and she fell between the standing upon the earth. And he searched for a long time; they hoped for the power of the end <note>possibly the "rest" or "cessation"</note>, that they might not believe in the flight; they were few and great and he was God. 

<gloss>7</gloss> As it happened, then, the drawing near of all of it in looking, how for one deed her salvation was simple. It became great and large. And it hinders the world in its time, their piling up <note>perhaps referring to the gathering of communal wealth</note>, powerfully. 

<gloss>8</gloss> They say then of her salvation: it is rich in all its power, she received in her power that which happened. And all in these things is her repayment and sacrifice. And he placed in their hearts as it happened, and they sealed it. 

<gloss>9</gloss> And in that which happened: even the matter of those things which were in him at the time of the bread <note>likely a reference to the Eucharist or the breaking of bread in Acts</note>, he was providing for them and overshadowing them. 

<gloss>10</gloss> And as it happened they received. And in our souls were those who said: "Be amazed!" 

<gloss>11</gloss> Our souls, then, without the oil of God; and our souls at the gate for our reception. That which turned away happened in it at the time. And as the hand of God was upon her. 

<gloss>12</gloss> He appeared on the rolling lips <note>Possibly a poetic way to describe speaking or the turning of a scroll</note>. And holy are the punishments of God. 

<gloss>13</gloss> And from what they said, he was renewed: and he gives life in his rolling life. And in one death, they received fear because of how it was. And they searched our piling up: as if in him he clothed the sealed rolling [one]. 

<gloss>14</gloss> And we found them as they are. And they sought from us: and how in his life the rolling punishment [is]. And we believed as if in him [is] life. 

<gloss>15</gloss> And in it, the hand of God strengthens us: they went out to the way in the sweet blood of the Son, the Savior, our Savior: and in prayer to the Living Father. And in it, her repayment is living: which was for the fathers and our brothers. 

<gloss>16</gloss> And they sought in life. And he brought out from the mountain in her repayment: that he might show how the Son [is]: because the element <term>esṭuksā; from the Greek "stoicheion," meaning a fundamental principle or a physical element</term> is that which belongs to her, which happened in him. ܀

<gloss>17</gloss> And from that which belongs to God, he stood before us: he sent this reward of hers in the life of descent. And in that which they sealed: as in that which happened. <gloss>18</gloss> They believed in him the Kingdom: the thing of the winter: he received that they did not find in him that there is something which remains in him of the Father.

### Acts of the Apostles 28 ###

...concerning the kingdom of God, testifying and persuading them about Jesus, from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets, from morning until evening. $^{24}$ And some of them were persuaded by his words, and others were not persuaded. $^{25}$ And they departed from him while not agreeing with one another. And Paul said this one word to them: “Well did the Holy Spirit speak through the mouth of Isaiah the prophet concerning your fathers, $^{26}$ when he said: ‘Go to this people and say to them: You shall surely hear but you shall not understand; and you shall surely see but you shall not perceive.’ <note>Paul is quoting Isaiah 6:9-10, a common passage used in the New Testament to explain why some rejected the Gospel message.</note> $^{27}$ For the heart of this people has grown dull, and their hearing is heavy, and they have closed their eyes; lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart and turn to me, and I should forgive them. $^{28}$ Be it known to you therefore, that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles <term>ʿammmē; literally "the nations," referring to non-Jewish peoples</term>. For they will also listen to it.” $^{30}$ And Paul stayed in his own rented house <note>original: "house of his own," implying he paid his own expenses even under house arrest</note>, and he was in it for two years. And he used to receive all those who came to him. $^{31}$ And he was preaching about the kingdom of God, and was teaching with boldness <note>original: "with openness/revelation"</note> everything concerning our Lord Jesus Christ <note>The OCR text reads "his holy soul," but this is a variant or scribal phrasing for the person of Christ or the Spirit's work</note> without hindrance.
