# ܀ The Epistle of James the Apostle ܀

<margin>
Chapter 1
For the Sunday
of the Infirm
<note>This marginal note indicates a liturgical rubric, showing that this specific passage was read in the church service on the Sunday dedicated to the sick or weak.</note>
</margin>

^1 James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered among the nations <note>original: "the peoples"</note>: Peace.

^2 Let it be all joy to you, my brothers, when you enter into various and many trials. ^3 For you know that the testing of faith gains you patience <term>msaybrānutā; endurance or steadfastness</term>. ^4 And let that patience have a perfect work, so that you may be complete and perfected, and lacking in nothing. ^5 If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all simply and without reproach, and it shall be given to him. ^6 But let him ask in faith, not doubting. For he who doubts is like the waves of the sea that are troubled by the wind. ^7 And let not that man think he will receive anything from the Lord, ^8 he who is divided in his mind <note>literally "double-minded" or "split in thought"</note> and troubled in all his ways.

^9 But let the humble brother boast in his high standing, ^10 and the rich in his humiliation, because like the flower of the grass, so he passes away. ^11 For the sun rises in its heat and withers the grass, and its flower falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So also the rich man fades in his ways. ^12 Blessed is the man who endures trials; for when he has been proven, he shall receive the crown of life, which God promised to those who love him. ^13 Let no man say when he is tempted, "I am tempted by God." For God is not tempted by evil things, and he tempts no man. ^14 But every man is tempted by his own desire, and is enticed and led away. ^15 And this desire conceives and gives birth to sin. And sin, when it is completed, gives birth to death.

^16 Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers. ^17 Every good and perfect gift descends from above, from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change, nor even a shadow of turning. ^18 He willed and gave birth to us <note>original: "begat us"</note> by the word of truth, that we should be the firstfruits of his creatures. ^19 And you, my beloved brothers, let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger. ^20 For the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God. ^21 Therefore, put away from you all filthiness and the abundance of wickedness, and in humility receive the word planted in our nature <note>The Syriac "kyānan" emphasizes the word being rooted in one's very being/nature</note> which is able to save your souls. ^22 But be doers of the word and not hearers only...

<summary>This page opens the Epistle of James, addressing the "twelve tribes" and offering encouragement to endure trials with patience and faith. It warns against the dangers of desire and anger while emphasizing that all good gifts, including the "word of truth," come from God.</summary>

<margin>Chapter 2</margin>
<gloss>1</gloss> My brothers, do not hold the faith of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ with partiality <note>original: "taking of faces," a common idiom meaning to judge by outward appearance or status</note>. <gloss>2</gloss> For if a man comes into your assembly with a gold ring on his hand, or in beautiful clothes, and a poor man comes in foul clothes; <gloss>3</gloss> and you look at him who is dressed in beautiful clothes and say to him, "You, sit here in a good place," and to the poor man you say, "You, stand over there," or "Sit here before the footstool of our feet"; <gloss>4</gloss> have you not become divided within yourselves and become judges of evil thoughts? <gloss>5</gloss> Listen, my beloved brothers. Do not the rich exalt themselves over you, and they drag you to the house of judgment? <gloss>7</gloss> Do they not blaspheme the good name that is called over you? <gloss>8</gloss> And if you fulfill the law of God in this, as it is written: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well. <gloss>9</gloss> But if you show partiality, you commit sin, and you are convicted by the law as transgressors of the law. <gloss>10</gloss> For whoever keeps the whole law and yet stumbles in one thing, is guilty of the whole law. <gloss>11</gloss> For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." But if you do not commit adultery but you do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law. <gloss>12</gloss> So speak and so act, as people who are going to be judged by the law of liberty. <gloss>13</gloss> For judgment is without mercy upon him who has not shown mercy. You exalt yourselves <note>or "triumph"</note> by mercy over judgment. <gloss>14</gloss> What is the use, my brothers, if a man says he has faith and has no works? Can his faith save him? <gloss>15</gloss> And if a brother or a sister should be naked and lacking daily food, <gloss>16</gloss> and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warm and be full," and you do not give them the needs of the body, what is the use? <gloss>17</gloss> So also faith without works is dead in itself.

->### ܀ The Epistle of James ܀<-

<margin>James 2</margin>
<sup>18</sup> Someone will say to them, "My brothers, you have faith <note>original: "mlamlana," literally a 'speaker' or 'wordy one,' but used here in place of the standard Peshitta 'haymanuta' (faith)</note>, and I have works." Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works. <sup>19</sup> You believe that there is one God; you do well. Even the demons <note>original: "sapra karka," likely a corruption of "shēdē" (demons)</note> believe and tremble greatly. <sup>20</sup> But do you want to know, O weak man, that faith without works is dead? <sup>21</sup> Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered Isaac <note>original: "aymani," likely a transcription error for "Isḥaq" (Isaac)</note> his son upon the altar? <sup>22</sup> You see that his faith helped his works, and by works his faith was made perfect. <sup>23</sup> And the scripture was fulfilled which says, "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness," and he was called the Friend of God. <sup>24</sup> You see then that a person is justified by works, and not by faith alone. <sup>25</sup> In the same way, was not Rahab the harlot also justified by works, when she received the messengers and sent them out by another way? <sup>26</sup> For as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.

---

<margin>Chapter 3</margin>
<sup>1</sup> Let not many of you become teachers, my brothers, for you know that we shall receive a stricter judgment. <sup>2</sup> For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in word, he is a perfect man, able also to bridle his whole body. <sup>3</sup> And if we put bits into the mouths of horses so that they may obey us, we turn their whole body. <sup>4</sup> Look also at the ships: although they are so large and are driven by fierce winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot's will desires. <sup>5</sup> So also the tongue is a small member and boasts of great things. See how great a forest is set on fire by a small flame! <sup>6</sup> And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity. The tongue is placed among our members as that which defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of our life <note>original: "ramḥa," likely referring to the 'wheel' or 'cycle' of nature/birth</note>, and is itself set on fire by Gehenna <note>the place of spiritual punishment</note>. <sup>7</sup> For every kind of beast and bird, of reptile and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by human nature. <sup>8</sup> But no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison. <sup>9</sup> With it we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse people who are made in the likeness of God. <sup>10</sup> Out of the same mouth proceed blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so. <sup>11</sup> Does a spring pour out from the same opening both fresh and bitter water? <sup>12</sup> Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce olives, or a grapevine produce figs? So neither can a salt spring produce fresh water. <sup>13</sup> Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show his works by his good behavior in the meekness of wisdom. <sup>14</sup> But if you have bitter jealousy and contention in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth. <sup>15</sup> This is not the wisdom that comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic.

<margin>Chapter 4</margin>
<sup>1</sup> For from what source come wars and strife among you? <sup>13</sup> Now then, we say to you who say: "Today or tomorrow we will go to such and such a city, and we will spend a year there, and we will trade and profit." <sup>14</sup> And they do not know what will happen tomorrow. Every boast like this is evil. <sup>17</sup> And he who knows the good and does it not, it becomes sin to him.

->### ܀ The Fifth Order ܀ 54<-

The world is the earth and the arena of training <note>original: "athleṭuta" — a term derived from the Greek word for athletics, used by Syriac authors to describe the rigorous spiritual struggle of monks and saints</note>. And like athletes we meet in it as in a battle for victories.
⁶ And we have been filled with strength; and defeat <note>original: "ḥubā" — literally "loss" or "defeat," often contrasted with "victory" in spiritual warfare</note> did not stand against us. ܀ ܀ ܀
<margin>The Fifth, 8</margin> ⁷ But if he descended to the cutting off and the darkness: in the likeness of the sons of men, and thus. Just as in righteousness and perfected works they shall go out and return; and from it, that is the kingdom: in the likeness that the Creator went out, into the structures and for the sake of the tempter <note>original: "makshānā" — one who causes stumbling or a tempter</note>. ⁸ And again, even if he descended, and the darkness: and at the gates of Gehenna they began. The person <note>original: "parṣopā" — face, countenance, or person</note> who is beyond comprehension. ⁹ That which we knew from the world did not seem like us. For if it is not from that, even if his soul is helped—the soul of our brothers. ¹⁴ A strong soul. She is the living one: a full soul. ¹⁵ She is the recompense of heaven that descends: and the hidden and the chaste manifestation: and obedience reaches to the heaven of the Lord. ¹⁶ And by the labor of the one who atones, he is not found, not even in this earth. And our Lord is not Paradise. She who brings forth buildings <note>or "structures/creations"</note> is not abandoned to her. ¹⁷ But to the fifth, the recompense from the world is left to her: because something descended for her. For also her companion stood for her, who is the enemy from the world: because she feared if it were so. ¹⁸ And even if the world went out, sin went out to her. ¹⁹ And in prayer we meet defeat; the water heals. And he does not live for God; fulfill the number of life. ²⁰ From health he speaks, from the recompense. ²¹ If also it reaches from the blessed one: like the recompense of sin from the blessed one: speak from health: and all the lips of the kingdom. ܀

And his voice like the voice of many waters. ^16^ And he had in his right hand seven stars. And from his mouth went out a sharp sword with two edges. And his appearance was like the sun shining in its strength. ^17^ And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead; and he placed upon me his right hand, saying: Do not fear. I am the First and the Last. ^18^ And the Living One; and I was dead; and behold, I am alive forever and ever, Amen. And I have the keys of death and of Sheol <note>original: "šyōl" — the realm of the dead or the grave</note>. ^19^ Write therefore what you saw, and those things which are, and those which are to happen after these. ^20^ The mystery of the seven stars which you saw on my right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands which you saw are the seven churches.

# ܆ Paul the Apostle ܆

## ܆ The Epistle to the Romans ܆

<margin>Chapter 1</margin> ^1^ Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ <note>original: *Meshiḥa* — the Anointed One</note>, called and an apostle, who was set apart for the Gospel of God. ^2^ Which he promised from of old through his prophets in the Holy Scriptures, <margin>of life</margin> ^3^ concerning his Son, he who was born in the flesh from the seed of the house of David. ^4^ And he was known as the Son of God with power and by the Holy Spirit, who rose from the place of the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord. ^5^ Through him we have received grace and apostleship among all the nations <note>original: *‘amame* — meaning the Gentiles or non-Jewish peoples</note>, so that they might be obedient to the faith of his name. ^6^ Among whom you also are called in Jesus Christ. ^7^ To all those who are in Rome, beloved of God, called and holy. Peace and grace be with you from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ. ^8^ First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is heard of in all the world. ^9^ For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I always remember you in my prayers. ^10^ And I entreat that if now at last a way might be opened for me by the will of God to come to you. ^11^ For I greatly long to see you and to give you a gift of the spirit, that by it you may be strengthened. ^12^ And that together we may be comforted by the faith that is both yours and mine.

---

^13^ Now I want you to know, my brothers, that many times I intended to come to you, but I was prevented until now, so that among you also I might have fruit <note>The Syriac *adsha* can mean "kind," "sort," or "fruit/harvest" in a metaphorical sense.</note>, just as among the rest of the nations. ^14^ Greeks and barbarians, the wise and the foolish; I am obligated to preach to everyone. ^15^ And so I am eager to preach the good news to you who are in Rome also. ^16^ For I am not ashamed of the Gospel, because it is the power of God for the life <note>original: *ḥaye* — also translated as "salvation"</note> of everyone who believes in it, whether of the Jews first, or of the Arameans <note>original: *Armaye* — In the Syriac Bible, "Arameans" is the standard translation for "Greeks" or "Gentiles."</note>. ^17^ For the righteousness of God is revealed in it from faith to faith, as it is written: "The righteous shall live by faith." ^18^ For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all the iniquity and wickedness of men, those who hold the truth in iniquity. ^19^ Because the knowledge of God is manifest in them; for God has manifested it in them. ^20^ For the hidden things of God from the foundation of the world are understood and seen by means of the creatures <note>meaning the created things of the world</note>, even his power and his eternal divinity, so that they might be without an excuse <note>literally "without a word in the spirit" or defense</note>. ^21^ Because they knew God and did not glorify him as God.

# The Revelation of John

<margin>Chapter 4</margin> ¹ After these things I looked, and behold, a door was opened in heaven. And that first voice that I heard was like a trumpet <note>original: "ṣiporā" — literally a bird or whistle, but used here for the clear, piercing sound of a trumpet blast</note> speaking with me, saying, "Come up here, and I will show you what must happen." ² And immediately I was in the Spirit. And behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat upon the throne. ³ And he who sat was in appearance like a stone of jasper and of sardius. And a rainbow <note>original: "qaštā" — literally "the bow," referring to the rainbow as a sign of the covenant</note> of vision was around the throne, in appearance like an emerald. ⁴ And around the throne were twenty-four thrones. And upon those twenty-four thrones sat twenty-four elders <note>original: "qašišē" — can be translated as elders, priests, or presbyters; representing the leaders of the people of God</note>, clothed in white garments, and on their heads were crowns of gold.

⁵ And from the throne proceeded lightnings and voices and thunders. And seven lamps of fire burned before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God. ⁶ And before the throne was a sea of glass, which is like ice. And in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures <note>original: "ḥaywān" — living beings or beasts, often identified in tradition as the cherubim or symbols of the four Evangelists</note>, full of eyes in front and behind. ⁷ And the first creature was like a lion. And the second creature was like a calf. And the third creature had a face like a human being. And the fourth creature was like a flying eagle.

⁸ And each of these four creatures stood, and each had six wings. And from within they were full of eyes. And they have no rest day or night, saying, "Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who comes." ⁹ And whenever the creatures give glory and honor and thanksgiving to him who sits on the throne, to him who lives forever and ever, amen. ¹⁰ The twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne and worship him who lives forever and ever. And they cast their crowns before the throne, saying: ¹¹ "Worthy are you, our Lord and our God, to receive glory and honor and power, because you created everything, and by your will they existed and were created."

¹ And I saw on the right hand of him who sat on the throne a book <note>original: "ktābā" — a scroll or book, representing the destiny of the world</note> written on the inside and on the back, and sealed with seven seals. ² And I saw another powerful angel proclaiming with a loud voice, "Who is worthy to open the book and to loosen its seals?" ³ And no one was able, neither in heaven nor on earth nor under the earth, to open the book, nor even to look at it. ⁴ And I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the book, nor even to look at it. ⁵ And one of the elders said to me, "Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed. He shall open the book and its seven seals."

⁶ And I saw in the midst of the throne and of the four creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb <note>original: "emrā" — a young sheep; a central title for Christ in the book of Revelation</note> standing as if slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God that are sent out into all the earth. ⁷ And he came and took the book from the right hand of him who sat on the throne. ⁸ And when he took the book, the four creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each having a harp <note>original: "kenārā" — a stringed instrument like a lyre</note> and golden bowls <note>original: "zaburā" — vessels or censers</note> full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. ⁹ And they sang a new song, saying, "Worthy are you to take the book and to loosen its seals, because you were slain, and you redeemed us..."

# To the Romans: Chapter 5

<margin>Chapter 5</margin>
¹ Therefore, having been justified <note>original: "etza-daqnan" — a legal term meaning to be declared righteous or acquitted in a court of law</note> by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. ² Through him we have been brought by faith into this grace in which we stand; and we boast in the hope of the glory of God. ³ And not only so, but we also boast in our afflictions <note>original: "ulṣanayn" — refers to trials, pressures, or tribulations faced by the early community</note>, for we know that affliction produces patience in us; ⁴ and patience, experience; and experience, hope. ⁵ And hope does not put us to shame, because the love of God is poured out upon our hearts by the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. ⁶ For if, because of our weakness, Christ at this time died for the sake of the wicked— ⁷ for hardly does a man die for the sake of the righteous; though for the sake of the good, perhaps someone might dare to die. ⁸ Here God shows his love toward us: for if, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us, ⁹ how much more, then, shall we now be justified by his blood, and through him be saved from wrath? ¹⁰ For if, while we were enemies, God was reconciled with us through the death of his Son, how much more, then, in his reconciliation, shall we live by his life? ¹¹ And not only so, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

# ܀ To the Romans 8 ܀

<margin>Chapter 8</margin> <note>original: "Cap. viii" — Latin abbreviation for "Capitulum," meaning Chapter.</note> $^1$ Therefore, there is now no condemnation to those who do not walk according to the flesh, in Jesus Christ. $^2$ For the law of the Spirit of life which is in Jesus Christ has freed you from the law of sin and of death. $^3$ For because the law was weak through the infirmity of the flesh, God sent His Son in the likeness of the flesh of sin. And because of sin, He condemned sin in His flesh, $^4$ so that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us—we who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit. $^5$ For those who are in the flesh think on the things of the flesh, and those who are of the Spirit think on the things of the Spirit. $^6$ For the thought of the flesh is death, and the thought of the Spirit is life and peace. $^7$ Because the thought of the flesh is enmity toward God; for it is not subject to the law of God, because it is not able to be. $^8$ And those who are in the flesh are not able to please God. $^9$ But you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if truly the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if a person does not have the Spirit of Christ, this one does not belong to Him. $^{10}$ And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness. $^{11}$ And if the Spirit of Him who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead dwells in you, He who raised Jesus Christ from the dead will also give life to your dead bodies, because of His Spirit that dwells in you.

### The Thirty-Fourth Discourse ###

<sup>7</sup> What then? That which the element <note>original: "estuksa" — from the Greek *stoicheion*, referring to the basic components or forces of the physical and spiritual universe.</note> created was not entrusted. But how is the making? Where are the distinctions <note>original: "peruse" — This term literally means "Pharisees" or "Separated Ones," but in this philosophical context, it likely refers to "Distinctions," "Explanations," or perhaps "Selected Entities."</note> where its work is in its work? <sup>8</sup> But the people whom I have numbered, whom God gave to them to be governors for the animals <note>original: "ḥaywātā" — can mean "living creatures" or "animals," often used allegorically to represent the lower, non-rational nature.</note>, they shall not be tested by them. It is right for us that they should serve in the likeness of the animals that existed. <sup>9</sup> And the children <note>original: "derdeqe" — literally infants or small children; here likely referring to simple believers or those new to spiritual knowledge.</note> say again: let there be distinctions from them alone, and distinctions for the higher things. <sup>10</sup> They shall descend to the lower things and shall not see. And those who see the distinction shall be united. <sup>11</sup> They say: they are not those who were saved in everything just as they fell. They see: but in both places, that living one belongs to the higher things, to the distinction. <sup>12</sup> And if it was spoken to them in both in the world, then the lives which are in both in the world and the fruits are their end.

<sup>13</sup> He examined them, they say, not for the higher things. But it was known through them for the higher things, because a woman <note>Likely an allegorical reference to Wisdom or the Soul.</note> was found among them. <sup>14</sup> For in everything, he was entrusted to the creatures in love, and those things which come out from them. <sup>15</sup> If their service lives, so that they were saved in this world, it cuts off the distinctions; but the living one went out from among the dead. <sup>16</sup> If, then, the body remains, so also do the creatures. This one is after the first; also the fools <note>original: "sakhle" — refers to those lacking spiritual insight or the "ignorant."</note>. <sup>17</sup> If then the fools who were saved, and those other things which were saved in those days, then the likeness of the end is in the world and in the love of others <sup>18</sup> who were saved among the fools. But if there is a service, it is not like the lives within the world, but it is after that which is pleasing to him. <sup>19</sup> And in everything that was said, that folly was saved; and those in their days were saved. <sup>20</sup> Well. And he spoke of lives—and in what way? That they were saved. As for their testing from here: let him not draw near in sin, but she feared. <sup>21</sup> If testing was found among the fools, they do not see that in everything joy was spoken in the world. <sup>22</sup> The living one who said: let them save it and its distinction of destruction. But it was found that he went out. Stature <note>original: "qawmātā" — a term often used in Syriac mysticism to describe spiritual heights or levels of being.</note>. But in the world they shall save it, if the testing in it is similar. Not this: <sup>23</sup> as there are those who were saved. And as for the fear, if he does not save among the animals and their distinction, they also shall be saved. They are saved before God who said: "Let there be lives." <sup>24</sup> If they live as he said, how is it as she said: he who led her so that they were saved? And without testing they were saved in the world of fear. It stood, and these are its fruits, if it was known from them in the world of animals.

<sup>25</sup> I desire it to be known: that he fears—in what way? Only this: that they shall not be saved by the work; they shall save, that he may live. Because concerning both, within the body, he spoke that it was for a likeness; in the likeness of the work, it is known in the distinctions. <sup>26</sup> And the boundary <note>original: "tuḥāmā" — a limit, definition, or boundary line.</note> before the living element that I numbered: that the will of the distinctions might be set right in it, and he gave it to all his children. <sup>27</sup> And the boundary of destruction was in that which was given from all that I numbered, when the animals went out in it. <sup>28</sup> But after that, the creatures are foul; they are known. And in what manner are they saved from them? <sup>29</sup> For God is not again in her salvation, in salvation.

-> ### Of Luke the Evangelist ### <-

Or even a person who truly dies for a person. In life, but not to the Lord, for he lives without anything that is separate, in that which is in the good bitterness. ¹⁵ If because of something his feeling is evil to a person, his feeling is not for the immortality of the person. <margin>Chapter 2</margin>
$^1$ And I, my brothers, when I came to you, did not come with grand speech or wisdom when I proclaimed to you the mystery of God. $^2$ And I did not judge <note>In this context, "judge" means "to resolve" or "to decide."</note> within myself to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and him even as crucified. $^3$ And I was with you in great fear and in trembling. $^4$ And my word and my proclamation were not with the persuasiveness of words of wisdom, but with the demonstration of the Spirit and of power, $^5$ so that your faith would not be in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God. $^6$ However, we do speak wisdom among the perfect <note>Referring to those who are spiritually mature or fully initiated into the faith.</note>—a wisdom not of this world, nor of the rulers of this world who are passing away. $^7$ But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery—that which was hidden, and which God had predestined from before the worlds for our glory.

<summary>Paul rebukes the Corinthians for their internal divisions and argues that true divine wisdom is found in the "foolishness" of the cross, which upends human social and intellectual hierarchies. He emphasizes that his own preaching relied not on eloquent philosophy but on the power of the Spirit.</summary>

For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed for us. <gloss>8</gloss> Therefore, let us keep the festival, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of wickedness and bitterness, but with the leaven of purity and holiness.

<gloss>9</gloss> I wrote to you in an epistle not to associate with the sexually immoral. <gloss>10</gloss> I did not mean, however, the sexually immoral of this world, or the covetous, or the extortioners, or the worshippers of idols; otherwise, you would be obligated to depart from the world entirely. <gloss>11</gloss> But now I have written to you not to associate with anyone who is called a "brother" if he is sexually immoral, or covetous, or a worshipper of idols, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner. With such a person, do not even eat bread. <gloss>12</gloss> For what business of mine is it to judge those who are outside? Do you not judge those who are within? <gloss>13</gloss> But those who are outside, God judges. Therefore, remove the evil one from your midst.

### -> ܀ The First Epistle to the Corinthians, Chapter 7 ܀ <-

I wish that all people were like me in their conduct. However, each person has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that way. ⁷ I say then to those who have no wives and to widows, that it is better for them to remain as I am. ⁸ But if they cannot endure, let them marry, for it is better for them to take a wife than to burn with passion <note>original: "regtā" — refers to burning with desire or intense physical longing</note>. ⁹ To those who have wives I command—not I, but my Lord—that a woman should not separate from her husband. ¹⁰ And if she does separate, let her remain without a man, or be reconciled to her husband; and a man should not leave his wife. ¹¹ And to the rest, I say—not my Lord—if there is a brother who has a wife who does not believe, and she is willing to live with him, let him not leave her. ¹² And a woman who has a husband who does not believe, and he is willing to live with her, let her not leave her husband. ¹³ For the husband who does not believe is sanctified <term>sanctified: "mqaḏaš" — in this context, it means to be set apart or brought into a sphere of holiness through the family bond</term> by the wife who believes, and the wife who does not believe is sanctified by the husband who believes. Otherwise, your children would be unclean, but now they are pure. ¹⁴ But if the one who does not believe separates, let him separate. A brother or a sister is not enslaved in these matters. God has called us to peace. ¹⁵ For how do you know, O woman, if you will save <note>original: "taḥēn" — literally 'to give life' or 'to preserve'</note> your husband? Or you, O man, how do you know if you will save your wife? ¹⁶ But as the Lord has distributed to each, and as God has called him, so let him walk. And I command this in all the churches.

¹⁷ If you were circumcised <note>original: "gzīrā" — refers to the Jewish ritual of circumcision</note> when you were called, do not return to uncircumcision. And if you were called in uncircumcision, do not be circumcised. ¹⁸ For circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of God's commandments. ¹⁹ Let every person remain in the calling in which he was called. ²⁰ If you were called as a servant <term>servant: "ʿabdā" — a common term for a slave or bondservant in the ancient world</term>, do not let it worry you. But even if you are able to be freed, choose rather to serve. ²¹ For he who was called in our Lord as a servant is the freedman of God. Likewise, he who was called as a free man is the servant of Christ. ²² You were bought with a price; do not become servants of men. ²³ Let every person, my brothers, remain with God in the calling in which he was called.

²⁴ Now concerning virgins <note>original: "btūlātā"</note>, I have no commandment from God. But I give counsel as a man who has received mercy from God to be faithful. ²⁵ And I think this is good, because of the necessity of the time <note>original: "ananqē d-zabnā" — refers to the "present distress" or the difficult period the early Christians believed they were living in</note>, that it is better for a person to remain as he is. ²⁶ Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife. ²⁷ But if you take a wife, you have not sinned; and if a virgin is married to a man, she has not sinned. But those who are such will have affliction in the flesh; and I would spare you. ²⁸ And I say this, my brothers, that the time henceforth is short. Let those who have wives be as though they had none, ²⁹ and those who weep as though they did not weep, and those who rejoice as though they did not rejoice, and those who buy as though they did not possess.

<header>### ܀ The Narrative of His Dispensation ܀</header>

³¹ And those who use this world, let it be in this manner: not as if they were fully using it. For the form <term>form: "eskāmā" — refers to the outward appearance or temporary fashion of the world</term> of this world is passing away. ³² Because of this, I desire that you be without anxiety. For he who is without a wife is concerned with the things of his Lord, ³³ while he who has a wife is concerned with the things of the world, how he may please his wife. ³⁴ There is a distinction between a wife and a virgin. She who is without a husband is concerned with her Lord, that she may be holy in her body and in her spirit. But she who has a husband is concerned with the world, how she may please her husband. ³⁵ This I say for your own benefit; I am not laying a snare for you, but so that you may be constant before your Lord in a beautiful manner, while not being distracted by the world. ³⁶ But if anyone thinks that he is shamed regarding his virgin daughter, because her time has passed, and he has not given her to a husband, and it is right that he should give her—let him do what he desires; he does not sin. Let them be married. ³⁷ But he who has firmly decided in his heart, and is not pressured by necessity, and has authority over his own will, and has judged this in his heart, to keep his virginity, he does well. ³⁸ And he who gives his virgin daughter does well, but he who does not give her does even better. ³⁹ A wife is bound by the law as long as her husband lives. But if her husband should sleep <note>original: "nevdak" — a common New Testament euphemism for death</note>, she is free to be married to whomever she wishes, but only in our Lord. ⁴⁰ But she is more blessed if she remains as she is, according to my own opinion. And I think that I also have the Spirit of God within me.

### Of the Fifth Day

<margin>Chapter 8</margin>
¹ Now concerning the time of the offerings <note>original: "pērāwātā" — literally "fruits," but used here in the context of sacrifices or offerings</note>, it is known that in all of us there is knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. ² If anyone thinks that he knows something, he does not yet know anything as he ought to know it. ³ But if anyone loves God, this person is known by Him. ⁴ Concerning the eating of the offerings of the righteous <note>The text here uses "righteous" (zadīqē), likely a scribal variant or error for "idols" (ptakrē) which is standard in this verse</note>, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God except one. ⁵ For even if there are those called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, as there are many gods and many lords, ⁶ yet for us, we have one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we are in Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we are through Him. ⁷ However, not everyone has this knowledge. For there are some who, in their conscience until now, eat it as something offered to idols; and because their conscience is weak, it is defiled. ⁸ But food does not bring us near to God. For if we eat, we gain nothing, and if we do not eat, we lack nothing. ⁹ But take care that this liberty <note>original: "msaybrānūṯā" — endurance or patience, used here in the sense of one's right or authority to act</note> of yours does not become a stumbling block to the weak. ¹⁰ For if someone sees you, you who have knowledge, reclining in the house of idols, will not his conscience, because it is weak, be encouraged to eat that which is offered to idols? ¹¹ And by your knowledge, he who is weak—the brother for whose sake Christ died—is destroyed. ¹² And if in this way you sin against your brothers and wound their weak consciences, you are sinning against Christ. Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I do not cause my brother to stumble.

## ܀ The First Epistle to the Corinthians, Chapter 9 ܀

<margin>Chapter 9</margin> <sup>1</sup> Am I not free? Or am I not an <term>apostle: "shlikhā" — one sent as a messenger or representative</term>? Or have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Or are you not the work of my labor in the Lord? <sup>2</sup> Even if I am not an apostle to others, yet I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship. <sup>3</sup> This is my defense <note>original: "mappaq berukhā" — literally a 'spiritual defense' or an 'answer' given to critics</note> to those who judge me. <sup>4</sup> Do we not have the authority to eat and to drink? <sup>5</sup> And do we not have the authority to lead about a sister <note>The Syriac "khātā" (sister) here refers to a Christian wife or a female believer who assists in the ministry</note> as a wife with us, like the rest of the apostles, and like the brothers of our Lord, and like <term>Cephas: "Kephā" — the Aramaic name for the Apostle Peter, meaning 'Rock'</term>? <sup>6</sup> Or is it only I and Barnabas who do not have the authority to refrain from manual labor? <sup>7</sup> Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Is God concerned only for oxen? <sup>10</sup> Rather, it is known that He said it for our sakes; indeed, for our sakes it was written, because it is right for him who plows to plow in hope, and for those who tread grain to do so in the hope of the harvest. <sup>11</sup> If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it a great thing if we reap physical things from you? <sup>12</sup> And if others have this authority over you, do we not have it even more? But we have not used this authority. Instead, we endure everything so that the <term>Gospel: "sebartā" — literally 'the good news' or 'the message'</term> of Christ might not be hindered in anything. <sup>13</sup> Do you not know that those who work in the sanctuary are sustained by the provisions of the temple? And those who serve at the altar share in the offerings of the altar? <sup>14</sup> In the same way, our Lord commanded that those who preach His Gospel should live from His Gospel. <sup>15</sup> But I have not used any of these rights. And I have not written this so that it should be done this way for me. For it would be better for me to die than for anyone to make my boasting void. <sup>16</sup> For even though I preach, I have no reason to boast. For necessity is laid upon me; and woe to me if I do not preach! <sup>17</sup> For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward. But if it is not of my own will, I am entrusted with a <term>stewardship: "rabat baytutha" — the management or administration of a household</term>. <sup>18</sup> What then is my reward? That when I preach, I might make the Gospel of Christ available without expense, and not use the authority given to me in the Gospel. <sup>19</sup> For while I am free from all men, I have enslaved myself to all men, that I might gain many. <sup>20</sup> And I became like a Jew to the Jews, that I might gain the Jews. And with those who are under the Law, I was as if I were under the Law, that I might gain those who are under the Law. And those who are [not] under the Law...

# ### ܀ Laws and Regulations ܀

You must distinguish between the animals: between the clean and the unclean. You shall not defile your souls with animals, or with birds, or with anything that creeps on the earth, which I have separated for you to be considered unclean. <note>The Syriac text here paraphrases Leviticus 20:25, emphasizing the spiritual "defilement of the soul" through dietary choices.</note> <sup>21</sup> And you shall not deliver your souls over to any of the swarming things that creep upon the earth. You shall be holy, for I, the Lord, am holy. <sup>22</sup> A path and a voice are prepared for their salvation; for you, there is a path of the voice and of the mountains. <note>original: "ba-qālā" — this refers to a 'voice' or 'sound,' perhaps suggesting a prophetic call or liturgical response.</note> <sup>23</sup> What have you commanded, holy neighbors, that a holy voice should be heard by me? <sup>24</sup> No, I have not commanded you [burdensome] commands. No, I have not commanded you dwellings of negligence. <sup>25</sup> I seek from you prayers, and that you fear me, and hear my words, and be holy. <sup>26</sup> Just as I am holy, says the Lord. <sup>27</sup> When you are in the land of Canaan <term>Canaan: the ancient name for the region that became the Land of Israel</term>, the land of the kingdom: <sup>28</sup> If any man among you sells a house in a city surrounded by a wall, he shall have the right to redeem it until the year of its sale is completed. <sup>29</sup> But if he has not redeemed it by the time the year is finished, the house in the city shall belong to its buyer throughout the generations. <sup>30</sup> But if a house is in a village that has no wall, it shall be considered like the open field of the land. <sup>31</sup> A right of redemption shall remain for it, and in the Jubilee <note>original: "yōbelā" — the Year of Jubilee occurred every 50 years, a time when debts were forgiven and land returned to its original owners</note> it shall be released. <sup>32</sup> It is necessary for you, my beloved ones, to turn away from all excessive festivals; let prayers and vigils be performed instead. <sup>33</sup> For it is said by me: I am the Lord your God.

<margin>Chapter 11.</margin> <sup>1</sup> A prayer [to be said] before the time of dawn. <sup>2</sup> Because the Lord said to Moses, to say to the children of Israel: When you enter the land of inheritance that I give to you, <sup>3</sup> you shall rejoice to eat the fruits within it.

<sup>3</sup> The land shall be for you an inheritance, which I give to you. <sup>4</sup> When you plant all kinds of food, you shall pick their fruits in the years I give to you. <sup>5</sup> In the fourth year, it shall be holy to the Lord. <sup>6</sup> You shall not work the land in the seventh year <note>The Sabbatical year (Shmita), where the land is left to rest and no farming occurs</note>, as I told you. <sup>7</sup> When you are in the land of inheritance, do not sow your field with all [mixed] seeds. <sup>8</sup> Do not sow your field with two kinds of seeds. <sup>9</sup> Do not sow your field with three kinds of seeds. <sup>10</sup> Do not sow your field with four kinds of seeds. <sup>11</sup> In the fifth year, you shall eat their fruits. <sup>12</sup> When you enter the land of which I spoke to you, which I give to you as an inheritance: <sup>13</sup> And when you harvest the harvest of your land, do not finish [reaping] the very edge of your field. <sup>14</sup> And do not gather the gleanings of your harvest. <note>This refers to the practice of 'Peah,' leaving the corners of the field for the poor and the stranger.</note>

He teaches his household: the reward of when his old age remains <note>original: "qā'em saḇūṯeh" — literally "his old age stands," referring to a state of being or a lasting legacy in one's later years</note>, she desired it. <sup>15</sup> And the reward of when his old age arrived, it was delayed for her, because his old age instead turned to another in it. <sup>16</sup> If the first man entered upon us, his own children did not belong to her, and she did not cause them to perish.

<margin>17</margin> <margin>Of Life</margin> But he who hungers does not. Not even if he is poor does he hunger. Because it was not in her faith that she was changed, <margin>18</margin> but her strength was in her firmness. He who does not even have an edge from it does not possess fruit. He was guilty <margin>31</margin> in her time, and he did not even possess it, because he did not distinguish the fruit of the word. ### ܀ Similitudes of Mortals, Chapter 40 ܀

I am among you: of the house of the fathers of Abraham the Deacon <note>original: "mšamšānā" — a term for a deacon or one who serves in the church</note>; and he said, "This is how I served." And there is no deacon in Paradise whose service is comparable, except in the Spirit and Holiness. <sup>3</sup> There are various kinds of **workings**, but it is the same Spirit. <sup>4</sup> And there are various kinds of **service**, but it is the same Lord. <sup>5</sup> And there are various kinds of powers <note>original: "mḥaylūṯā" — literally "strengths" or "powers," though in some contexts it can refer to the working of miracles</note>, but it is the same God who performs everything in everyone.

<sup>6</sup> To each person, the manifestation of the Spirit is given for their benefit. <sup>7</sup> To one is given through the Spirit the **word of wisdom**. To another, the **word of knowledge** by that same Spirit. <sup>8</sup> To another, **faith** by that same Spirit. To another, **gifts of healing** by that same Spirit. <sup>9</sup> To another, **miracles**; to another, **prophecy**; to another, the **discernment of spirits**; to another, various **kinds of tongues**; and to another, the **interpretation of tongues**. <sup>10</sup> One and the same Spirit performs all these things, distributing to each person just as it wills.

<sup>11</sup> For just as the **body is one** and has many members <note>original: "hadāmē" — limbs, organs, or parts of the body</note>, and all the members of the body, though they are many, are one body—so also is Christ. <sup>12</sup> For we were all baptized by one Spirit into one body, whether Jews or Arameans <note>original: "armāyē" — often used in the Peshitta to mean Gentiles or Greeks</note>, whether slaves or free; and we have all been made to drink of one Spirit. <sup>13</sup> For the body is not one member, but many.

<sup>14</sup> For if the **foot** should say, "Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body," it is not because of this that it is not part of the body. <sup>15</sup> And if the **ear** should say, "Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body," it is not because of this that it is not part of the body. <sup>16</sup> If the whole body were an **eye**, where would the hearing be? And if the whole were **hearing**, where would the sense of smell be? <sup>17</sup> But now, God has placed each one of the members in the body just as He willed. <sup>18</sup> If they were all one member, where would the body be? <sup>19</sup> But now, the members are many, yet the body is one.

<sup>20</sup> The **eye** cannot say to the **hand**, "I have no need of you," nor again can the **head** say to the **feet**, "You are not necessary to me." <sup>21</sup> Rather, those members that are thought to be weak are the ones most needed. <sup>22</sup> And those we think are less honorable in the body, we clothe with greater honor. And those that are unseemly, we dress with greater beauty. <sup>23</sup> But those members among us that are glorious do not require honor. For God has tempered the body and given greater honor to the member that is small, <sup>24</sup> so that there may be no **division** <note>original: "palgūṯā" — schism, division, or discord</note> in the body, but that all members should care for one another equally. <sup>25</sup> So that when one member suffers, all the members suffer. And if one member is glorified, all the members rejoice with it. <sup>26</sup> Now you are the **body of Christ**, and members <sup>27</sup> in your place.

<margin>Chapter 13</margin> <sup>1</sup> If I should speak in every tongue of men and of angels, but have not **love** <note>original: "ḥubbā" — the Syriac word for love, corresponding to the Greek "agape"</note>, I have become as sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. <sup>2</sup> And if I should have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I should have all faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. <sup>3</sup> And if I should feed the poor with everything I own, and if I should hand over my body to be burned, but have not love, I gain nothing. <sup>4</sup> Love is patient in its spirit and it is kind; love does not envy; love is not agitated, nor is it puffed up with pride. <sup>5</sup> It does not commit shameful acts, nor does it seek its own; it is not provoked, nor does it plot evil. <sup>6</sup> It does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices in the truth. <sup>7</sup> It endures all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and bears all things. <sup>8</sup> Love never fails; for prophecies shall cease, and tongues shall be silenced, and knowledge shall pass away. <sup>9</sup> For we know but a little of much, and we prophesy but a little of much. <sup>10</sup> But when perfection comes, then that which is but a little shall pass away. <sup>11</sup> When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I reasoned as a child, and I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I set aside the things of childhood. <sup>12</sup> For now we see as if in a mirror, in a dark riddle <note>original: "pelmā" — a shadow, image, or riddle; referring to an obscure or indirect vision</note>, but then we shall see face to face. # ܀ The First Epistle to the Corinthians ܀

^18 And he conducted it so that it might resemble kinship <note>original: "ʿemāmāyutā" — referring here to a shared nature or ethnic commonality.</note> (protecting it in this). ^19 This is not in three or in two, but in one; thereafter is the proclamation of kinship, that we might live like the Father who was before them.

^20 And it came to pass that the departure was before the ranks <note>original: "pandē" — a term often used for ranks, divisions, or successive groups.</note>, and that the finding of the likeness occurred. ^21 For as by man came death, so also by man shall be the resurrection of the dead. ^22 For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ they live. ^23 As in Adam they die, so also in Christ they live in ranks. There is a departure in his knowledge (just as the blood of Christ is their kinship). ^24 And you shall know where the one is, he who delivers the kingdom to God the Father, when he shall have abolished all principalities and all authorities and powers. ^25 All is one. For he was destined to reign in his knowledge, as the Word of God is before them; where they are before them. ^26 And the last enemy to be abolished is death. ^27 For he has put all things under his feet. But when it says that everything is subjected to him, it is evident that it is God who subjected all to him. ^28 And when all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all. ^29 Otherwise, what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead do not rise at all, why are they baptized for the dead?

As it is written: "The first man Adam became a living soul." ^45 And so, the last Adam became a life-giving spirit. ^46 But the spiritual was not first; rather, the natural <note>original: "napshānāyā" — literally "soulish" or pertaining to the physical life-force</note> was first, and then the spiritual. ^47 The first man was from the earth, of dust; the second man is from heaven. ^48 As is the one of dust, so also are those of dust; and as is the one from heaven, so also are those of heaven. ^49 And as we have worn the likeness of the one from dust, so shall we wear the likeness of the one from heaven. ^50 But this I say, my brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven, nor does corruption inherit incorruption. ^51 Behold, I tell you a mystery <term>mystery: "rāzā", a hidden divine truth now being revealed</term>. # The Second Epistle to the Corinthians, Chapter 11 <note>original: "22" — The Syriac heading uses the number 22, likely referring to a specific lection or section in this manuscript's tradition, though the text corresponds to the modern Chapter 11.</note>

<margin>21</margin> ²¹ I speak as if in shame, as though we were weak. In whatever anyone else dares to boast—I speak in foolishness—I also dare to boast. ²² Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? So am I. ²³ Are they ministers of Christ? I speak in foolishness: I am more than they; in labor more than they, in stripes more than they, in imprisonments more than they, in deaths many times.

<margin>25</margin> ²⁴ From the Jews five times I received forty stripes minus one <note>According to Jewish Law (Deuteronomy 25:3), a person could not be beaten more than 40 times; 39 was the standard to avoid accidentally exceeding the limit.</note>. ²⁵ Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I suffered shipwreck. A night and a day I have been in the deep without a ship. ²⁶ In many journeys, in dangers of rivers, in dangers of robbers, in dangers from my own kindred, in dangers from the Gentiles, in dangers in the city, in dangers in the wilderness, in dangers in the sea, in dangers among false brothers; ²⁷ in toil and weariness, in many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, in many fastings, in cold and nakedness. ²⁸ Besides the external things, there is that which crowds upon me daily: the care for all the churches.

<margin>30</margin> ²⁹ Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn? ³⁰ If I must boast, I will boast in my infirmities. ³¹ The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever and ever, knows that I do not lie. ³² In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas <term>Aretas: Aretas IV, the King of the Nabataeans who ruled Damascus during Paul's stay.</term> guarded the city of the Damascenes to seize me. ³³ And through a window in a basket they let me down from the wall, and I escaped his hands.

<margin>Chapter 12</margin> ¹ It is necessary to boast, though it is not profitable. For I come to visions and revelations of our Lord. ² I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago—whether in the body or out of the body, I do not know, God knows—who was caught up to the third heaven. ³ And I know this man—whether in the body or out of the body, God knows— ⁴ that he was caught up into Paradise and heard words that cannot be spoken, which it is not lawful for a man to utter. ⁵ Of such a one I will boast, but of myself I will not boast, except in my infirmities. ⁶ For if I desire to boast, I shall not be a fool, for I speak the truth. But I refrain, lest anyone should think of me more than what they see in me or hear from me. ⁷ And lest I should be exalted by the abundance of revelations, a thorn was given to me in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to buffet me, so that I would not be exalted. ⁸ For this thing I besought my Lord three times, that he would remove it from me. ⁹ And he said to me: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is perfected in weakness." Gladly, therefore, I will boast in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

# ܀ The Epistle to the Galatians ܀ #

<margin>Chapter 1</margin>
<margin>New <unclear>Life</unclear></margin>
<sup>1</sup> Paul, an apostle—not from men and not through a son of man, but through Jesus Christ and God his Father, who raised him from the house of the dead— <sup>2</sup> and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia. <sup>3</sup> Grace be with you, and peace from God the Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ, <sup>4</sup> who gave himself on behalf of our sins to deliver us from this evil world, according to the will of God our Father, <sup>5</sup> to whom be glory forever and ever, Amen.

<sup>6</sup> I am amazed at how quickly you are turning away from Christ, who called you by his grace, to another gospel <note>original: "ewangelyon" — a direct loanword from the Greek 'euangelion'.</note>, <sup>7</sup> which does not even exist! However, there are people who trouble you and wish to change the gospel of Christ. <sup>8</sup> But even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you anything other than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed <term>original: "khrem" — related to the concept of 'Anathema' or something set apart for destruction</term>. <sup>9</sup> As I said before and now I say again: if anyone preaches to you anything other than what you have received, let him be accursed. <sup>10</sup> For now, do I persuade men or God? Or do I seek to please men? For if until now I were pleasing men, I would not be a servant of Christ.

### ->܀ To the Galatians [Chapter] 2 ܀<- ###

^11 But when Cephas <note>original: "Kipa." This is the Aramaic/Syriac name for the Apostle Peter, meaning "Rock" or "Stone."</note> came to Antioch, I rebuked him to his face, because he was found to be in the wrong. ^12 For before certain men came from the presence of James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they came, he withdrew and separated himself, because he was afraid of those who were of the circumcision <note>This refers to Jewish Christians who believed that non-Jewish converts must follow Jewish ceremonial laws, such as circumcision and dietary restrictions.</note>. ^13 And the rest of the Jews also joined him in this hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was led away by their partiality. ^14 But when I saw that they were not walking uprightly according to the truth of the Gospel, I said to Cephas before them all: ^15 "If you, being a Jew, live like the Gentiles and not like the Jews, how do you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?" ^16 For we, who are Jews by nature and not "sinners" from among the Gentiles, ^17 know that a man is not justified <note>In this context, "justified" means to be made right or declared righteous before God.</note> by the works of the <term>Law</term> <note>The Law (Syriac: Namusa) refers to the Torah or the Mosaic Law given to Israel.</note>, but by faith in Jesus Christ; even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the Law. ^18 Because by the works of the Law no flesh shall be justified. ^19 But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are also found to be sinners, is Jesus Christ then the minister of sin? God forbid! ^20 For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I show myself to be a transgressor of the commandment. ^21 For I, through the Law, died to the Law, that I might live to God. ^22 And I am crucified with Christ; and from now on it is not I who live, but Christ who lives in me; and that which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved us and gave himself for our sake. ^23 I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the Law, then Christ died in vain.

### ->܀ To the Galatians [Chapter] 3 ܀<- ###

<margin>Chapter 3</margin> ^1 O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you? For behold, before your very eyes Jesus Christ was portrayed as being crucified. ^2 This only I want to learn from you: Did you receive the Spirit from the works of the Law, or from the hearing of faith? ^3 Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now finished in the flesh? ^4 Have you suffered all these things in vain—if indeed it was in vain? ^5 He therefore who gives the Spirit to you and works miracles among you, does he do it by the works of the Law, or by the hearing of faith? ^6 Just as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. ^7 Know then that those who are of faith, these are the children of Abraham. ^8 For because God knew beforehand that the Gentiles would be justified by faith, he previously gave the good news to Abraham, as the Holy Scriptures say: "In you shall all the nations be blessed." ^9 Therefore, those who are believers are blessed along with Abraham the believer. ^10 For those who are of the works of the Law are under a curse; for it is written: "Cursed is everyone who does not perform all that is written in this Law." ^11 But that no man is justified by the Law before God is evident, because it is written: "The just shall live by faith." ^12 But the Law is not of faith; rather, "He who does these things that are written in it shall live by them."

<summary>Paul describes his public disagreement with Peter (Cephas) regarding Jewish and Gentile relations, arguing that righteousness comes through faith in Christ rather than adherence to the Mosaic Law. He uses the example of Abraham to show that the blessing of faith precedes the Law.</summary>

# To the Galatians [Chapter] 3 #

$^{13}$ Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the <term>Law</term> <note>The Law (Syriac: *Namusa*) refers to the religious and social regulations given to Israel through Moses.</note>, and he became a curse for our sake. For it is written: "Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree." $^{14}$ This was so that the blessing of Abraham would be among the nations through Jesus Christ, and that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. $^{15}$ My brothers, I speak as among the sons of men: when a man's covenant has been confirmed, no one rejects it or adds anything to it. $^{16}$ Now the promises were promised to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say to him "to your seeds," as if speaking of many, but "to your seed," as if speaking of one, who is Christ. $^{17}$ And I say this: the covenant which was previously confirmed by God in Christ, the Law—which came four hundred and thirty years later—does not reject it or nullify the promise. $^{18}$ For if the inheritance is from the Law, then it is no longer from the promise. But God gave it to Abraham by promise. $^{19}$ Why then the Law? It was added because of transgression, until the "seed" should come to whom the promise belonged. And the Law was given through angels by the hand of a mediator. $^{20}$ Now a mediator is not for one person alone, but God is one. $^{21}$ Is the Law then against the promise of God? Far be it! <note>original: *Ḥas*. This is a strong idiomatic expression meaning "By no means" or "God forbid."</note> For if a law had been given that was able to give life, then righteousness would truly have come from the Law. $^{22}$ But the Scripture has shut up everything under sin, so that the promise through faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

# ܀ To the Galatians [Chapter] 5 ܀ #

⁴ You have been severed from Christ, those of you who seek to be justified by the <term>Law</term> <note>Syriac: *Namusa*, referring to the Mosaic Law.</note>; you have fallen away from grace. ⁵ For we, through the Spirit, eagerly await the hope of righteousness which comes from faith. ⁶ For in Christ Jesus, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision carries any weight; rather, it is faith that is made complete through love. ⁷ You were running well! Who hindered you from obeying the truth? ⁸ This persuasion does not come from Him who called you. ⁹ "A little leaven leavens the whole lump." <note>A common ancient proverb used to warn that a small amount of error can corrupt an entire community.</note> ¹⁰ I have confidence in you in our Lord, that you will not think otherwise; and he who troubles you will bear his judgment, whoever he may be. ¹¹ But as for me, my brothers, if I still preached circumcision, why would I still be persecuted? ¹³ For you, my brothers, were called to freedom; only do not let your freedom become an opportunity for the flesh, but serve one another in love. ¹⁴ For the whole Law is fulfilled in one word, namely: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself." ¹⁵ But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another! ¹⁶ I say then: Walk in the Spirit, and you will not satisfy the lust of the flesh. ¹⁷ For the flesh desires that which harms the Spirit, and the Spirit desires that which harms the flesh; these are opposed to each other, so that you do not do the things that you want. ¹⁸ But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the Law. ¹⁹ For the works of the flesh are well-known, which are: fornication, impurity, indecency, ²⁰ idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, anger, selfishness, divisions, factions, ²¹ envy, murder, drunkenness, revelry, and everything similar to these. And I tell you now, as I told you before: those who practice such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God. ²² But the <term>fruit of the Spirit</term> <note>Paul contrasts "works" (plural) of the flesh with a single "fruit" (singular) of the Spirit, suggesting a unified character.</note> is: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, ²³ humility, and self-control. Against such as these, the Law is not set. ²⁴ And those who belong to Christ have crucified their flesh with all its passions and desires. ²⁵ Let us live, therefore, in the Spirit, and let us submit to the Spirit. ²⁶ Let us not be vain-glorious, provoking one another and envying one another.

Was it not with those who sinned and whose bones fell in the desert? <sup>17</sup> And concerning whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, if not those who were not persuaded? <sup>18</sup> And we see that they were not able to enter because they did not believe. <sup>19</sup> Let us fear, therefore, lest while the promise of entering into his rest stands, anyone among you be found remaining from entering. <sup>20</sup> For we also have been brought the good news just as they were; but the word they heard did not profit them, because it was not mixed with faith for those who heard it. <sup>21</sup> But we enter into rest, we who have believed, as he said: "As I swore in my anger, they shall not enter my rest." <sup>22</sup> For behold, the works of God have existed from the beginning of the world.

<sup>1</sup> Therefore, because of this, let us not remain at a standstill; that now we may enter his rest, let each of you be found ready beforehand. <sup>2</sup> For we also have been evangelized just as they were. ^3 I thank my God for your remembrance always, ^4 and in all my prayers on your behalf; and while I rejoice, I make supplication ^5 regarding your fellowship in the Gospel <note>original: "ܐܘܢܓܠܝܘܢ" (ewangelyon), a loanword from the Greek 'euangelion' meaning 'Good News.'</note> from the first day until now. ^6 Because I am confident in this: that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. ^7 For it is right for me to think this about all of you, because you are placed in my heart. <margin>Chapter 2</margin>
^1^ If, therefore, you have any comfort in Christ, and if there is any speech in love that is pleasant, and if there is any fellowship of the Spirit, and if there are any mercies and compassions, ^2^ fulfill my joy: that you may be of one mind, and one love, and one soul, and one thought. ^3^ And do nothing through contention or through empty glory, but in humility of mind, let each person consider his neighbor as better than himself. ^4^ And let no man satisfy only his own needs, but let every man also care for his neighbor. ^5^ And think this within yourselves, that which was also in Christ Jesus: ^6^ He, while he was in the likeness of God, did not consider it a thing to be seized <note>original: "ܚܛܘܦܝܐ" (khutupya), meaning a "snatching" or "theft," translating the Greek 'harpagmos.' It suggests Christ did not feel he had to "grasp" at equality with God because it was already his.</note> that he was the equal of God. ^7^ But he emptied himself <note>original: "ܣܦܝ" (sap-pi), literally "poured out." This is the theological concept of 'kenosis,' where Christ sets aside his divine privileges.</note> and took the likeness of a servant, and was in the likeness of the sons of men; and in fashion, he was found as a man. ^8^ And he humbled himself and was obedient unto death—even the death of the cross. ^9^ Because of this, God has also greatly exalted him, and given him a name which is more excellent than all names; ^10^ that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow—of those in heaven, and on earth, and those under the earth— ^11^ and every tongue shall confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God his Father.

^12^ Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed—not only when I am near to you, but now that I am far from you—much more so, with fear and with trembling, work for the salvation of your souls. ^13^ For it is God who encourages in you both to will and to do that which you desire. ^14^ Do everything you do without grumbling and without division, ^15^ so that you may be perfect and without blemish, like the children of God who dwell in a crooked and perverse generation; and appear among them like lights in the world, ^16^ as you hold fast to the word of life <note>original: "ܟܐܡܐ ܕܚܝܐ" (kyama d-khaye). ### ܀ The Theology of Saint Di... <note>Likely Saint Dionysius the Areopagite, a 5th-6th century mystical theologian whose works were widely translated into Syriac.</note> ܀ ###

In only two dispositions <note>original: "mṣaybānātā" — referring to the internal states or compositions of a person.</note>, as the servant of God distinguishes, and which are preserved in the body; just as they are for the creatures and the possessions which are common to them, and the precious, holy soul of the Lord. It is also within her, as if for the creation of God and the precious, holy soul.

<margin>Chapter 2</margin>
$^{1}$ However, its primary will <note>original: "ṣebyānā" — a central concept in Syriac theology referring to the intentionality or free will of the soul.</note> is above all the long-suffering <term>endurance</term> <note>original: "etnaggartā" — often refers to patient endurance or the stretching out of the spirit.</note> of the precious holy soul, and of our Savior who is in both [natures]. $^{2}$ For she was not troubled by her creation, nor did she find rest except in Him, the Fountain. Neither did her spirit stand [still], nor did the Divinity stand [apart], as if the will were led by them; this is with all the obligation <note>original: "ḥawbā" — can mean debt, sin, or duty; here it implies a spiritual obligation.</note> of the precious one. $^{3}$ In faith, the will desired that her obligation be fulfilled through Him; but the speaker <note>Likely referring to the rational faculty of the soul.</note> was not saved except by being guided in faith. And the preservation was by means of the Sun of Joy and the boundary. $^{4}$ It happens that salvation occurred. And the Recipient stood over all, so that in the wonder that belongs to them and to us, even the "cooking" <note>original: "bušālā" — a technical term in Syriac mysticism meaning "ripening" or "maturation" of the soul toward God.</note> of God might be returned as God’s, and might show concerning His will that it became as God’s. $^{5}$ Not through faith alone did the will lead them, but in order to show [the way] through them alone. $^{6}$ And the faithful are known to be those who are led in His likeness. $^{7}$ For if the holy body did not stand in faith, then in its rest, how would the Disposer <note>original: "mṣaybānā" — one who orders or arranges, often referring to God or the higher soul.</note> stand according to her will? $^{8}$ And the believer is exalted above all. It happens that the precious soul shall glorify Him with her mouth, and all souls with the zeal of the boundary. $^{9}$ And her endurance is in that same faith which confirms all life. And thus, she is in distinction. $^{10}$ And when the duality of what happens in both is not found, it is because you did not receive the life and the faithful one through whom we live. $^{11}$ Because of this, He shall save through them where the divine operation <note>original: "maʿbdānutā" — the 'energy' or 'working' of God.</note> is, which is by means of the Sun of Heaven. $^{12}$ And especially the body of Christ, which without doubt is in distinction (but He willed that everything be returned). $^{13}$ One, however, is the living things in the distinction of God, but the body of Christ is not in the mercy of the precious one. And the passing over of God stood for the sake of Heaven in mercy, in the distinction that was not in the faith of Heaven. $^{14}$ Because He did not will it to be in two. But the will of the precious soul of Christ, which belongs to the Savior (but so that a person might return to holiness), $^{15}$ shall confirm how [this is]. And the will of the precious, holy soul shall come. $^{16}$ For the precious, holy soul of God exists in distinction, and of man, and as if for the creation of God and the precious, holy soul. $^{17}$ In every will of the precious, holy soul. And He shall save every body, and everything that is in Him.

<margin>Chapter 3</margin>
$^{1}$ Now He has placed the Spirit of the precious, holy soul so that she might be a participant in everything that is in her. $^{2}$ And He shall direct the holy body in faith, and our Savior who is in both. $^{3}$ But in faith is the will of the precious, holy soul, and the protection of the Divinity; and He shall save the holy one. $^{4}$ But how is it only from the obligation of the precious, holy soul? And the recipient of the things of heaven is also in distinction. $^{5}$ And this will shall be returned, so that as God [wills], it shall be returned.

$^5$ Now the goal of the commandment is love that comes from a pure heart, from a good conscience <note>original: "reʿyānā ṭāḇā" — literally a "good mind" or "good thought," used here to denote a clear conscience.</note>, and from true faith. $^6$ And from these things, some men have strayed and turned aside to empty words. $^7$ They desire to be teachers of the law, yet they do not understand what they are saying, nor the things about which they contend. $^8$ But we know that the law is good if a man is guided by it as the law intended, $^9$ knowing that the law was not set for the righteous, but for the wicked and the rebellious, for the ungodly and the sinners, for the profane and for those who are not holy, for those who strike their fathers, and for murderers, $^{10}$ for fornicators, for those who lie with males, for those who steal free men <note>original: "gannāḇay bnay nasha" — literally "thieves of the sons of men," referring to kidnappers or slave-traders.</note>, for liars, for those who swear false oaths, and for everything that is contrary to the sound teaching $^{11}$ of the Gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was entrusted to me. $^{12}$ And I thank him who has strengthened me, our Lord Jesus Christ, who considered me faithful and appointed me to his service— $^{13}$ I, who was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insider of insults. # Theology of the Faith

## ܀ The Third Discourse on the Faith ܀

<margin>Chapter 1</margin>
¹ The peaceful division of the holy names <note>original: "shmāhē mqadshē" — this likely refers to the distinct names of the persons of the Trinity.</note>, by the sight of God and by the gift of the grace of His Holy Spirit. ² In that new strength, regarding the second [part], both the new and the ancient things stood before God the Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.

³ We confess <note>original: "mawdēnan" — this is the standard opening for a formal creed or statement of belief.</note> then that great and true God, whose primordial generation is not from human origins; we also confess the birth of God in unity. ⁴ It came to be, yet not through [mere] human thought. ⁵ We confess then the undivided condition <note>original: "aykanāyutā" — a technical term meaning 'quality' or 'mode of being'.</note>, in its own kind along with the consolations of life; that which is a creation in the place where the consolations and decrees of the Living One are constant, yet it is not named like the whole of it. ⁶ For this reason, His Lordship is not limited, which is the "mingling" <term>mingling: Syriac "muzāgā" usually refers to a union. In this theological context, it describes how the divine and human are united in Christ without being confused or lost.</term> of God, which is above all these things. ⁷ For it is not because the Son of God became a judgment that He was without power, nor that the power became Lordship. ⁸ One should not be moved by the support of the "Name of Life," <note>original: "shmā d-ḥayē" — a common Syriac epithet for the divine life or Christ himself.</note> but rather by all things, without any inequality of will in you, and that which belongs to Him in the power of God. ⁹ And just as our Lord was distinct in His life like all others, yet as one in [eternal] life; and to abolish [the idea] that His divinity—in which all the holy ones [dwell]—is subject to any destruction or created work. ¹⁰ And that He rested in it perfectly, a life-giving and holy gift, which in its entirety is a single, ineffable gift and renewal in its very nature. ¹¹ And His divinity is in it as a third kind, yet not a divided kind. ¹² Therefore His Lordship is beyond thought and beyond the [earthly] consolation of life. For life is not indeed in its entirety and peaceful [therein]. It is divided, yet it lives in its nature on every side. Consider that consolation. ¹³ How then is it not so? Because of their lives, the divided [nature] is seen in the condition and the "leaning" of the five holy ones. <note>This may refer to the five senses or perhaps five specific Church Fathers or witnesses mentioned in the tradition.</note>

And it is not a small thing to receive His divinity. ¹⁷ But also in human things, in the unity of the Son and Christ. ¹⁸ It shall live for Him, that we might name the grace of the heart from that consolation, and however much it is divided before them.
