### The Second Epistle to Timothy

<margin>Chapter 3 <note>original: "Cap. iii." in Latin</note></margin>
^1^ But know this: that in the last days, hard times will come. ^2^ And people will be lovers of themselves and lovers of money, boastful, proud, blasphemous, and disobedient to their parents; they will be ungrateful, wicked, ^3^ and without natural affection <note>original: "pkihay qasta" — literally "cold of heart" or lacking family love</note>, slanderers, uncontrollable, fierce, and haters of the good. ^4^ They will be traitors, headstrong, puffed up with pride, and lovers of pleasures more than the love of God. ^5^ They will have a form of the fear of God <note>This refers to an outward appearance of piety or religious ritual.</note>, but they will be far from its power. Turn away from those who are like this. ^6^ For among them are those who creep from house to house and captivate women who are burdened with sins and led away by various lusts, ^7^ who are always learning and yet never able to reach the knowledge of the truth. ^8^ But just as Jannes and Jambres <note>According to Jewish tradition, these were the names of the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses in Pharaoh's court.</note> stood against Moses, so also these men stand against the truth—men whose minds are corrupted and who are rejected from the faith. ^9^ But they will not proceed further, for their folly shall be known to everyone, just as the folly of those others was also known. ^10^ But you have followed my teaching, and my conduct, and my purpose, and my faith, and my longsuffering, and my love, and my patience, ^11^ and my persecutions and my sufferings—those things that happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, and in Lystra <note>These were cities in Asia Minor (modern-day Turkey) where Paul faced violent opposition during his missionary journeys.</note>. What persecution I endured! And from all of them my Lord delivered me. ^12^ Indeed, all those who desire to live in the fear of God in Jesus Christ will be persecuted. ^13^ But evil men and deceivers will increase in their wickedness, deceiving and being deceived. ^14^ But you, remain in those things which you have learned and of which you have been assured, for you know from whom you learned them, ^15^ and that from your youth you have known the Holy Books <note>original: "Saphra Qadisha" — referring to the Hebrew Scriptures/Old Testament.</note>, which are able to make you wise unto life through faith in Jesus Christ. ^16^ Every scripture that was written by the Spirit is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness, ^17^ so that the man of God may be perfect and complete for every good work.

^5^ ...they were submissive to their husbands in every evil thing <note>original: "ṣebwātā bīšātā" — likely a commentary on the consequences of not following the instructions for wives mentioned in the epistle</note>; regarding those who are around them, even if they hear and fulfill what their husbands command as we have been instructed. ^6^ In this way, there would be no blasphemy <note>original: "ṣeḥnā" — meaning reproach or foul smell, used here for blasphemy</note> against the word of God wherever it is. ^10^ For there are many who are unsubmissive, and their words are empty, and they deceive the minds of men, especially those who are of the circumcision <note>Refers to Jewish converts who insisted on following the Mosaic Law as a requirement for Christianity</note>. ^11^ These are the ones whose mouths it is necessary to stop. For they subvert many houses and teach things which are not proper for the sake of filthy lucre <note>original: "yutrāne ṭenpe" — shameful or dirty profit</note>. ^12^ One of them, a prophet of their own <note>Historical note: This is a reference to the Cretan philosopher Epimenides</note>, said: "The Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and idle bellies." ^13^ And this testimony is truly [given]. Because of this, rebuke them sharply so that they may be sound in the faith, ^14^ and may not give heed to Jewish myths and the commandments of men who hate the truth. ^15^ For everything is pure to the pure. But to those who are defiled and do not believe, nothing is pure to them; rather, their mind and their conscience are defiled. ^16^ They profess that they know God, but by their works they deny Him; and they are hateful and disobedient, and rejected for every good work.

<margin>Chapter 2</margin> ^1^ But you, speak what is proper for sound doctrine. ^2^ And teach that the elders should be vigilant in their minds, and should be sober, and should be modest, and should be sound in faith, in love, and in patience. ^3^ And likewise the elderly women, that they should be in a demeanor that is proper for the fear of God. They should not be slanderers <note>original: "ākelqarṣā" — literally 'eaters of pieces', a common Syriac term for accusers or devils</note>, and they should not be enslaved to much wine, and they should be teachers of good things. ^4^ And let them train the young women to love their children and their husbands, ^5^ and to be sober and holy, and to care well for their homes and be submissive to their husbands, so that no one may blaspheme against the word of God. ^6^ And in the same way, urge the young men to be sober. ^7^ In everything, show yourself as an example in every good work; and in your teaching, let your integrity be seen as sober and faithful. ^8^ And let your word be sound, so that no one may reject it; so that those who stand against us may be ashamed, when they cannot find anything hateful to say against us.

10 And they were not seasoned <note>original: "malliḥīn" — likely an allusion to being "seasoned with salt" or wisdom; see Colossians 4:6</note>: (not true life, nor the good among the perfect goods: of nobility, in thoughts), but the blessing of the perfect Godhead. 11 That if we cross over to the faith of the Godhead which is united in three true **Persons** <term>qnōmē: the Syriac term for distinct 'substances' or 'hypostases' within the Trinity</term>. 12 And regarding this, it is not: that they might bring forth the spirituality and the primacy of the creation: of the creation: and it lived in this world in the likeness, and in the comprehension, and in the divine life: 13 while we bear the life-giving child <note>original: "šabrā" — can mean child or babe, here likely referring to the Incarnate Word</note> and the wisdom of the divinity of God and the perfect power given to power. 14 For he became the giver of himself as teacher: that he might provide for all from the beginning: and that he might shine in himself to the new world, the power of the believers of the heart. 15 And to the one speech and heart, and the **Person** <term>parṣōpā: often used for 'person' or 'countenance,' here emphasizing the distinct identity within the Godhead</term> of the distinct Name. ->To Philemon<-

# The Epistle to Philemon

^1 Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy the brother, to Philemon the beloved and our fellow worker, ^2 and to Apphia the beloved, and to Archippus our fellow worker, and to the church that is in your house. ^3 Grace be with you and peace from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.

^4 I give thanks to my God at all times, and I remember you in my prayers, ^5 behold, since I heard of your faith and the love which you have toward our Lord Jesus and toward all the saints; ^6 that the fellowship of your faith may yield fruit <note>original: "yāhbā pē’rē" — literally "giving fruits," implying a productive or active faith</note> in good works and in the knowledge of all the good things you have in Jesus Christ. ^7 For we have great joy and consolation, because by your love the hearts <note>original: "raḥmē" — literally "mercies" or "bowels," traditionally viewed as the seat of deep emotion and compassion</note> of the saints were refreshed.

^8 Because of this, I have great boldness in Christ to command you those things that are right. ^9 But because of love, I truly beseech you—I, Paul, who am an old man <note>original: "sbā" — an elder or aged person</note> as you know, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ. ^10 And I beseech you for my son, whom I have begotten in my bonds, ^11 **Onesimus** <note>The name Onesimus in Greek means "useful" or "profitable." Paul makes a wordplay on this name in the following sentence.</note>, he who at one time was of no use to you, but now is very useful both to you and to me. ^12 And I have sent him to you; but you, receive him as if he were my own heart <note>original: "ḥaššaw" — literally "my sufferings" or "my internal organs," expressing the deepest personal affection</note>.

^13 For I wished to keep him with me, that he might serve me in your stead in the bonds of the Gospel. ^14 But without your counsel I did not wish to do anything, so that your good deed would not be as if by compulsion, but by your own will. ^15 For perhaps also because of this he departed for a time, that you might possess him forever; ^16 no longer as a servant <term>ʿabdā: a term for a slave or bondservant in the ancient world</term>, but more than a servant, a brother beloved to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in our Lord.

^17 If therefore you are a partner to me, receive him as if he were me. ^18 And if he has deprived you of anything or owes you, count this to me. ^19 I, Paul, have written it with my own hands: I will repay it. (Lest I say to you that you owe even your own soul to me). ^20 Yes, my brother, let me be refreshed by you in our Lord; refresh my heart <note>original: "raḥmē" — see note on verse 7</note> in Christ. ^21 Because I am confident that you will listen to me, I have written to you; and I know that you will do more than what I say. ^22 At the same time also prepare for me a place to stay, for I hope that through your prayers I shall be given back to you.

^23 Epaphras, my fellow captive in Jesus Christ, greets you; ^24 and Mark, and Aristarchus, and Demas, and Luke, my helpers. ^25 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

To the Hebrews 1, 2

### The Epistle to the Hebrews

<margin>Chapter 1</margin> ^1^ In many parts and in many ways, God spoke with our fathers by the prophets from of old; ^2^ and in these last days, he has spoken with us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of everything, and by whom he made the worlds <note>original: "‘ālmē" — this can refer to both "worlds" in a physical sense and "ages" or "eons" in a temporal sense</note>; ^3^ who is the brightness of his glory and the image of his essence <note>original: "itūtā" — refers to the fundamental being or existence of God</note>, and holding all by the power of his word; and he, in his own person <note>original: "qnomā" — a technical term in Syriac theology referring to an individual nature or personhood, especially within the Trinity</note>, made the cleansing of sins and sat on the right hand of the Greatness in the heights. ^4^ And all this [he became] greater than the angels, just as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs. ^5^ For to which of the angels did God ever say, "You are my Son, today I have begotten you"? And again, "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son"? ^6^ But again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says, "Let all the angels of God worship him." ^7^ But concerning the angels he says thus, "Who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a burning fire." ^8^ But concerning the Son he says, "Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; a straight scepter is the scepter of your kingdom. ^9^ You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; because of this, God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy more than your companions." ^10^ And again, "You from the beginning laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands. ^11^ They shall pass away, but you remain; and they all shall grow old like a garment; ^12^ and like a cloak you shall fold them up; they shall be changed, but you are as you are, and your years shall not end." ^13^ But to which of the angels did he ever say, "Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies as a footstool beneath your feet"? ^14^ Are they not all spirits of service, who are sent for service on behalf of those who are to inherit life?

### The Third Work

The Lord did not leave her <note>Likely referring to the Church or the Soul, personified as feminine in Syriac</note> without making her known. But now, it was not in a new time that he showed her, as if she were something changed. 9 For he who spoke before through the angels showed her; that very one, the Savior, showed her in the likeness of one. And as for the rulers of the earth who were in name, he became the mediator of the earth’s reconciliation instead of the good Savior who makes [her] known. 10 When they were without a sender and without any kingdom, and all the work of hindrance to her reconciliation, because in the time of her joy he made them soulful. 11 It happens that those who were saved from the life of the vitality of their body, because of this, they are not held by her will. For when they found they could participate with the Judge, they were found in the defense of humanity. 12 And even though I am God, I turned to man; and although I am the one worshiped, I came so that I might go out to the gate through him. 13 For because humanity was condemned quickly and in opposition, so also the place of salvation became the place where the Creator was condemned. 14 So that in all the weariness of everyone, as it is spoken, the beauty of those who are the end might be seen. 15 And when we look at her building, it is found that in the life written in the Savior, their lives were left for eternity. 16 It was not as though an angel was being asked primarily, but concerning the ruler who was condemned, the question was asked. 17 For this reason also, it happened that in everything he left a legacy for life; he who showed the boundary of the children of the earth, making it known in the essence <note>original: "itūtā" — refers to fundamental being or existence</note>, and he who came as the Giver of Life to the vitality of the Church. 18 In that eye, behold, life was wrapped; he is glorified, those who were blotted out were wrapped in him.

<margin>Chapter 3</margin>
1 Therefore, my holy brothers, you who have been called with the calling that is from heaven, look at that Apostle and High Priest <note>original: "rab kumrē" — literally "chief of priests"</note> of our confession, Jesus Christ; 2 who is faithful to the one who made him, as was Moses in all his house. 3 For the glory of this one is much greater than that of Moses, just as the honor of the builder of a house is much greater than the building itself. 4 For every house is built by someone, but he who built all things is God. 5 And Moses was trusted in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken; 6 but Christ as a Son over his building. And we are his building, if until the end we hold fast to the boldness and the glory of its hope. 7 Because the Holy Spirit said: "Today, if you hear his voice, 8 do not harden your hearts to anger him, like the day of temptation in the wilderness, 9 where your fathers tempted me, and proved and saw my works for forty years. 10 Because of this, I was weary of that generation, and I said: 'They always err in their hearts, and they have not known my ways.' 11 And as I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter into my rest." 12 Look out, my brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, that departs from the living God. 13 But search yourselves <note>The Peshitta uses "nešta'al" (be asked/questioned/searched) where the Greek has "exhort one another"</note> every day, until the day which is called "Today," so that no one among you may be hardened by the deceptiveness of sin.

### To the Hebrews

¹⁴ For we have become partakers of Christ, if from the beginning until the end, we remain firm in this true faith. ¹⁵ As it is said: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts to provoke him." ¹⁶ For who were they who heard and provoked him? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt by the hand of Moses? ¹⁷ And with whom was he indignant for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned and whose corpses fell in the desert? ¹⁸ And to whom did he swear that they would not enter into his rest, if not to those who were disobedient? ¹⁹ And so we see that they were not able to enter because they did not believe.

->܀ ܀ ܀<-

<margin>Chapter 4</margin>
¹ Let us therefore fear, lest while the promise of an entrance into his rest remains, any of you should be found to fall short of entering. ² For we also have been brought the good news, just as they were; but the word they heard did not profit them, because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard it. ³ But we who have believed enter into the rest, as he said: "As I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter into my rest." For behold, the works of God have existed since the beginning of the world. ⁴ As he said concerning the Sabbath: "And God rested on the seventh day from all his works." ⁵ And here again he said: "They shall not enter into my rest." ⁶ Since, therefore, there was a place that individuals might enter, and those who were first brought the good news did not enter because they were disobedient, ⁷ he again appoints another day, after a long time; as it was written above that David said: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts." ⁸ For if Joshua <note>The Syriac text uses the name *Yishū‘ bar Nūn*, which is "Jesus son of Nun," the same name as Jesus of Nazareth. Most English Bibles clarify this as Joshua to distinguish the Old Testament leader.</note> son of Nun had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward concerning another day. ⁹ Therefore, a Sabbath-keeping <term>Sabbath-keeping: *shabbathutha*, referring to a state of rest modeled on the divine Sabbath</term> remains for the people of God. ¹⁰ For he who has entered into his rest has also rested from his own works, just as God did from his own. ¹¹ Let us therefore strive to enter that rest, so that we do not fall in the manner of those who were disobedient. ¹² For the word of God is living and all-working, and sharper than a two-edged sword; it enters even to the dividing of the soul and the spirit, and of the joints, the marrow, and the bones; and it judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart. ¹³ And there is no creature hidden from before it, but everything is naked and open before his eyes, to whom we give an account.

->܀ ܀ ܀<-

¹⁴ Since, therefore, we have a great High Priest <note>original: *rab kumre*, literally "Great of the Priests"</note> who has gone to heaven, Jesus Christ the Son of God, let us remain firm in his confession. ¹⁵ For we do not have a High Priest who is unable to feel with our weakness, but one who was tempted in everything just as we are, apart from sin. ¹⁶ Let us therefore draw near with an open countenance <note>A Syriac idiom meaning "with confidence" or "boldly"</note> to the throne of his grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace for a time of help.

# Hebrews Chapter 5

^1 For every <term>High Priest</term> <note>Syriac: Rab Kahna, literally "Great Priest"</note> who is appointed from among men stands on behalf of men in things pertaining to God, ^2 to offer offerings and sacrifices for himself, and to show compassion toward those who are ignorant and go astray, because he also is clothed with infirmity. ^3 And for this reason, he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, just as he does for the sake of the people. ^4 And no man takes this honor for himself, but only he who is called by God, just as <term>Aaron</term> <note>The brother of Moses and the first High Priest of Israel</note> was. ^5 So also, Christ did not glorify himself to become a High Priest, but rather it was He who said to him: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you." ^6 As He also said in another place: "You are a priest forever according to the likeness of <term>Melchizedek</term>." <note>original: "Malchizedek". A mysterious king and priest from Genesis 14, seen here as a "type" or foreshadowing of Christ's eternal priesthood.</note> ^7 Also, while he was clothed in flesh, he offered up prayers and supplications with a strong cry and with tears to Him who was able to save him from death, and he was heard. ^8 And although he was the Son, through the fear and the sufferings he endured, he learned obedience. ^9 And in this way he was perfected, and he became the cause of eternal life to all those who obey him. ^10 And he was named by God as the High Priest according to the likeness of Melchizedek. ^11 Now, concerning this Melchizedek, we have much to say, but it is difficult to explain because you have become dull in your hearing. ^12 For you ought to have been teachers, considering the time you have spent in the world; yet you have need to learn again what are the first words of the beginning of the oracles of God. You have become those who need milk, and not solid food. ^13 For everyone whose food is milk is not yet proficient in the word of righteousness, because he is an infant. ^14 But solid food is for the mature, those who, because of their practice, have their senses trained to distinguish between good and evil.

### -> Of the Existence of the Church, VIII <-

The sign of its existence is this: how, in the single existence of the Holy Lord who is not far off, and in the one way upon the mountain where they were comforted <note>Syriac: *atnaḥam*. ^1 For the Law had in it a shadow of the good things to come, but not the substance of the things themselves. # ܀ The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle ܀

<margin>Chapter 1</margin>
^1 Paul, called and an apostle <term>apostle: *shliha* — literally "one who is sent," acting as a formal representative or messenger with the sender's authority</term> of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother. ^2 To the church of God which is in Corinth—those who are called and holy in Jesus Christ, and to all those who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours. ^3 Grace <note>original: "taybuta" — divine favor or a gift given freely</note> be with you and peace from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ. ^4 I thank my God at all times on your behalf for the grace of God that has been given to you in Jesus Christ; ^5 for in everything you have been enriched in him, in every word and in all knowledge, ^6 just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed among you. ^7 Thus, you do not lack even one of his gifts, but you wait for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ, ^8 who himself will strengthen you until the end, so that you may be without blame in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. ^9 God is faithful, by whose hand you were called into the fellowship <term>fellowship: *shawtaphuta* — a word implying a deep, practical partnership, sharing, or communion</term> of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

^10 Now I beseech you, my brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that there be one word among you all, and that there be no divisions <note>original: "palguta" — schisms or split-factions</note> among you; rather, you should be perfect in one mind and in one thought. ^11 For it has been told to me about you, my brothers, by those of the house of Chloe <note>Chloe was likely a prominent woman in the early church whose household members or servants traveled and reported on the state of the Corinthian congregation.</note>, that there is strife among you. ^12 This is what I am saying: that there is someone among you who says, "I am of Paul," and someone who says, "I am of Apollos," and someone who says, "I am of Cephas" <note>original: "Kepha" — the Aramaic name for the Apostle Peter, meaning "Stone" or "Rock."</note>, and someone who says, "I am of Christ." ^13 Is Christ divided? Or was Paul crucified on your behalf? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul? ^14 I thank my God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius, ^15 so that no one can say I baptized in my own name. ^16 And I also baptized the household of Stephanas; otherwise, I do not know if I baptized any other person. ^17 For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the Gospel <note>original: "msabru" — to bring good news or announce glad tidings</note>; not with the wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made void.

<summary>Paul opens his letter to the Corinthians by addressing the report of internal factions and arguments over leadership. He emphasizes that the church's foundation is Christ alone, not the specific teachers who baptized or taught them.</summary>
<keywords>Paul, Sosthenes, Corinth, fellowship, Chloe, Apollos, Cephas, baptism, Gospel, unity</keywords>

# ->܀ The Revelation of John the Apostle ܀<-

...who is alive; and I was dead; and behold, I am alive forever and ever, Amen. And I have the keys of death and of Sheol <term>Sheol: *shiyul* — the place of the dead or the underworld, often synonymous with the grave in Syriac thought</term>. ¹⁹ Write, therefore, what you have seen, and those things which are, and those which are to happen after these. ²⁰ The mystery <term>mystery: *rāzā* — a secret, a symbol, or a hidden spiritual reality</term> of the seven stars which you saw on my right, and the seven golden lampstands. ²¹ The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.

<margin>Chapter 2</margin>

^1 Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to those who are called, who are beloved in God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ: ^2 Mercy and peace in love be multiplied to you. ^3 Beloved, while I was making every effort to write to you concerning our common life <note>original: *ḥayē gawnāyē* — literally "common lives," usually referring to general salvation or the shared Christian life</note>, I find it necessary to write to you and exhort you that you should contend for the faith which was once delivered to the saints. ^4 For certain men have crept in, those who were long ago marked out for this judgment, ungodly people who change the grace of our God into a state of filthiness <note>original: *ṣaḥnūṯā* — lewdness, filth, or indecency</note> and deny him who is the only Lord, our Lord Jesus Christ. ^5 I want to remind you, though you know all these things: that the Lord, after he had once saved the people out of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe. ^6 And the angels who did not keep their own headship <note>original: *rīšānūṯā* — authority, principality, or original domain</note> but left their own dwelling, he has kept in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day. ^7 Just as Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities, which in that same manner committed fornication and went after other flesh, are set as an example of eternal fire while they are condemned in judgment. ^8 In the same way also, these who are polluted in dreams defile the flesh, despise authority, and blaspheme against glory. ^9 But Michael the Archangel, when he was contending with the Accuser <term>Accuser: *ākelqarṣā* — the standard Syriac term for the Devil, literally meaning "eater of pieces" or "slanderer"</term> as he disputed about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a judgment of blasphemy against him, but said, "May the Lord rebuke you!" ^10 But these people blaspheme against things they do not know; And he said to me, “Take it and eat it; it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey.” 10 And I took the little book from the hand of the angel and I ate it; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey, but when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter. 11 And he said to me, “It is necessary for you to prophesy again concerning many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.”

And God, who brings forth divine powers by his hand. $^4$ And they received, as it were, a voice from heaven saying: "Depart from her in peace, so that you do not participate in her sins," because by a voice she was given over to her plagues. $^5$ For the sinners in her have reached up to heaven, and God has remembered their iniquities. $^6$ Repay her just as she herself repaid; double her portion, double for her deeds. In the cup that she mixed, mix for her double. $^7$ In everything that she glorified herself and lived in luxury, give her that much torment and mourning. Because she says in her heart, "I sit as a queen; I am no widow, and I shall see no mourning." $^8$ For this reason, in a single day her plagues shall come upon her: death, mourning, and famine. And she shall be burned with fire, for the Lord God is powerful. And the kings of the earth shall wail and weep for her—those who found rest with her and lived in luxury—when they see the smoke of her burning.

$^9$ While they stand far off <note>literally: "from opposite"</note> because of the fear of her torment, they shall say: "Woe, woe, great city! Babylon, the mighty city! For in a single hour your judgment has come." $^{11}$ And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her, and there is no one to buy their cargo anymore: $^{12}$ cargo of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; of fine linen <term>fine linen: known as byssus, a high-quality fabric used for royal garments</term>, purple, silk, and scarlet; and all scented wood, every ivory vessel, and every vessel of precious wood, brass, iron, and marble; $^{13}$ and cinnamon, spices, ointments, and frankincense; wine, oil, fine flour, and wheat; cattle, sheep, horses, and chariots, and the bodies within them <note>original: *gwayhun*—referring to the physical bodies of slaves or the "souls of men"</note>. $^{14}$ And the fruit-harvest of your soul’s desire has departed from you, and everything fat and beautiful has gone from you; you shall never see them again. $^{15}$ And they shall not find them again. And those who traded with her shall stand far off because of the fear of her torment, while they weep and mourn, $^{16}$ saying: "Woe, woe, great city, clothed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet, and adorned with gold, precious stones, and pearls!" $^{17}$ For in a single hour such great wealth has been laid waste. And all the shipmasters, and everyone who sails in ships to various places, and the sailors, and all who work on the sea, stood from a distance $^{18}$ and cried out as they saw the smoke of her burning, saying: "What city is like this great city?" $^{19}$ And they threw dust on their heads and cried out as they wept and mourned, saying: "Woe, woe, great city, in which all who had ships at sea became rich from her honor! For in a single hour she has been laid waste."

$^{20}$ Rejoice over her, O heaven, and you saints, apostles, and prophets! For God has judged your judgment against her. $^{21}$ And one of the mighty angels took up a great stone like a millstone <term>millstone: a massive, heavy stone used to grind grain; here it symbolizes a swift, sinking destruction</term> and threw it into the sea, saying: "Thus with violence shall the great city fall, and she shall never be found again. $^{22}$ And the voice of harpers, musicians, singers, and trumpeters shall not be heard in you again..."
